reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by new security bookkeeping, not by the older webhook route. The BIC itself created persistent Maps and fed them the raw request URL despite already having a canonical matched pathname. Because unauthorized failures were counted before authentication, an attacker needed only a reachable configured route and could vary the query to allocate indefinitely. The later file split preserved this exact behavior and is excluded as a refactor. The direct fix both canonicalized keys and bounded/pruned state, and release ancestry places it in 2026.3.1 but not 2026.2.26. Under the required BIC-commit-object-only rule, the human identities and complete absence of AI trailers or bot markers require NOT_AI regardless of any evidence outside that object.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The Zalo webhook handler resolved a registered target from URL.pathname, but then keyed process-global security-tracking maps with req.url, which includes the attacker-controlled query string. Repeated POSTs to one valid route with distinct queries therefore created distinct webhookStatusCounters entries even before authentication (the 401 path), and authenticated query churn likewise created distinct rate-limit entries and bypassed the intended per-route limit. Neither Map had a size bound or expiry, so a reachable webhook permitted unbounded memory growth and availability loss.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3 directly added webhookRateLimits and webhookStatusCounters to extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts, used req.url rather than the already-resolved pathname for status and rate-limit keys, and supplied no bound/expiry. The pre-existing webhook route itself predates this commit, but its immediate parent had none of this vulnerable tracking state. Commit 453664f09d0911cc1829d22c63f664f0ad2c8c10 later moved the same logic to monitor.webhook.ts without originating the flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated user who can create and execute workflows can stage a Git working repository whose configured push remote is another crafted local repository, then invoke the Git node's push or pushTags operation. Vulnerable releases permit the file transport for those write operations. The local git-receive-pack process runs receive-side hooks from the crafted target repository as the n8n process user. The earlier core.hooksPath=/dev/null mitigation protects hooks in the initiating working repository but does not suppress hooks in a local receive-pack target, so the result is arbitrary command execution on both self-hosted and cloud instances.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A plugin executing without PluginCapability.READ_FILES was supposed to be confined to the sandbox temporary directory and explicitly safe paths. The sandbox enforced that policy only by replacing builtins.open with restricted_open. Plugin code could instead import pathlib or io and call pathlib.Path.read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes/open or io.open; those independent entry points never reached restricted_open, so the plugin could read or modify arbitrary host files, for example Path('/etc/passwd').read_text(), despite lacking the file capability. The repository advisory specifically describes the bypass in threading mode and notes that process isolation had a separate broader restriction failure.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef is the smallest public first-writer: it creates plugin_sandbox.py and the plugin subsystem, advertises file-system capability enforcement, but _restrict_file_operations patches only builtins.open. Its single parent 649f737a9f04645508d079c0c772a8a2b4c7457a has no plugin_sandbox.py at the affected path. Later commits 642fb2bdec8af6f1d592c322dfa98647e145fcef, 35499f201ae2dc531d1194f6810c953d8b9af78b, and ccb60e1a29ef67700128ca54eb25a95413d71ff1 revise restoration, allowed-path context, and AST validation while retaining the builtins-only restriction, so they are carriers/hardening changes rather than introducers.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A repository-controlled .gitmodules section name is parsed unchanged by sm_name(), assigned to Submodule._name, and, on Git versions using gitfile submodules, joined to <parent git dir>/modules. A name containing ../ components therefore escapes that directory. During submodule initialization, GitPython creates parent directories and clones with --separate-git-dir at the escaped location, allowing a malicious repository whose otherwise tree-validated submodule path is legitimate to create and populate a Git repository at an attacker-chosen filesystem path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc introduced _need_gitfile_submodules() and _module_abspath(), whose modern-Git branch returned os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name), and changed update() to use that name-derived path for directory removal and Repo.clone_from(). The already-existing iter_items() flow obtained name by slicing the attacker-controlled .gitmodules section header with sm_name() and performed no validation. This commit created the first name-to-filesystem sink; later commit 67680a0877f01177dc827beb49c83a9174cdb736 refactored cloning into _clone_repo() and added --separate-git-dir but was not the first vulnerable implementation.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc states affected <=3.1.57 and patched >=3.1.58, identifies sm_name() -> Submodule._name -> _module_abspath() -> _clone_repo(), and records a released-3.1.57 PoC in which name '../../../../../../tmp/gitpython_poc_escaped_root/modules_dir' makes sm.update(init=True) create the escaped repository while core Git rejects the suspicious name.

Run `git show --format=fuller 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc -- git/objects/submodule/base.py`: the non-merge commit adds `_module_abspath`, returning `os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name)` for Git >=1.8, and changes update() from its checkout-path destination to `self._module_abspath(self.repo, self.path, self.name)` before cloning. `git show 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc:git/objects/submodule/base.py` lines around iter_items show `n = sm_name(sms)`, tree lookup by the separate `path`, then `sm._name = n`; util.py shows sm_name merely returns `section[11:-1]`.

Direct-parent proof: `git cat-file -p 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc` names sole parent a9a5414300a245b6e93ea4f39fbca792c3ec753f. `git grep -n -E '_module_abspath|separate_git_dir|git_dir.*modules|modules.*name' a9a5414300a245b6e93ea4f39fbca792c3ec753f -- git/objects/submodule` returns no matches, and the parent's update() uses `join_path_native(self.repo.working_tree_dir, self.path)` and clones there. Thus the immediate parent lacks the vulnerable name-derived module path.

Origin cross-check: `git log -L 304,313:git/objects/submodule/base.py 6e61b1d3bdcd2d9b81bac4eb4d17c18b270e5787` traces _module_abspath through formatting/type-only edits back to its addition in 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc; `git log --all --reverse -S'_module_abspath' -- git/objects/submodule/base.py` likewise identifies 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc as the first substantive addition. The commit has one parent and is not a move, revert, release commit, merge, or squash aggregate.

reasoning: Before the BIC, responseText was already intentionally raw HTML, but the completion response always received SANDBOX_CSP; therefore attacker script was confined to the sandbox rather than executing as the n8n origin. The BIC's security-relevant new behavior was specifically to omit that sandbox whenever the resolved respondWith value was redirect. Because renderFormCompletion still fetched and rendered responseText independently of respondWith, an expression-resolved redirect could coexist with stored raw HTML even though the editor's ordinary display rules presented those choices as mutually exclusive. Direct parent-tree inspection proves this exploitable combination did not exist one commit earlier, and -L/-S plus the 1.116.2-to-1.117.0 tag diff rule out a later move or backport as the origin. The August 2026 closing patch keeps redirects unsandboxed but removes their raw payload by setting responseText to the empty string unless showText is selected; the three maintenance-line tag diffs establish the final fixed boundaries. The BIC itself is authored by a named human, committed by GitHub, and has no commit-object AI marker. Bot authorship on the later bundled fix is irrelevant under the BIC-only attribution rule, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored same-origin XSS in the Form node completion page: renderFormCompletion always retrieved responseText and passed it to packages/cli/templates/form-trigger-completion.handlebars, whose triple-brace {{{responseText}}} sink rendered attacker HTML verbatim. Commit 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c changed the formerly unconditional sandbox Content-Security-Policy into a respondWith !== 'redirect' conditional without also suppressing responseText for redirect responses. An authenticated member could retain populated responseText while making the expression-capable respondWith parameter evaluate to redirect; a public-form submitter then received the raw HTML without the sandbox CSP, so script ran from the n8n origin with the visitor's session context.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest causal change is 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c (fix(n8n Form Node): CSP headers should not be set on response with redirect (#20864)). This newly created the exploitable combination; it is a focused two-file implementation/test commit, not a move, refactor, revert, release/backport, or broad squash aggregate.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated user who can run a workflow can supply crafted Edit Image / Draw Text input. The node line-wraps that value and passes it unchanged to gm.drawText(). gm 1.23.1 encloses text in an MVG quoted string and escapes double quotes but not attacker-supplied backslashes. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The @n8n/computer-use search_files tool accepted an attacker-influenced fast-glob pattern. It checked only the literal input for a leading slash or a slash-delimited '..' segment, then trusted fastGlob's expanded path strings for both filename results and content reads. A brace pattern such as '{a,..}/SECRET.txt' contains no literal '..' segment, passes assertPatternStaysInside(), but can expand to '../SECRET.txt'; path.join(resolvedDir, fp), fs.stat(), and fs.readFile() then access a file outside the configured base. An actor able to influence this tool call can disclose names and contents of arbitrary local files readable by the n8n daemon user.

reasoning: The authorization invariant before 7d6023f was conservative: every credential ID referenced by a node was checked against the workflow's accessible credential set. The BIC optimized away supposedly inactive credentials based on static parameter values, but expression parameters deliberately resolve later. Therefore a credential can be runtime-active and statically omitted, which is the advisory's root cause. The immediate parent lacks the filter and cannot take this bypass. PR #25599 is publicly decomposable: the first member writes all production logic and the second changes only a test, so using squash merge 608e3bf or later bundle 2d9a2ec as the BIC would be larger and causally late. The fix restores fail-closed behavior specifically at the static/runtime boundary by returning null for either expression-selected credential type, forcing every referenced credential ID through authorization. No qualifying AI evidence exists on the true BIC commit object, so the only supported closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated member who can edit a shared workflow can put a credential ID belonging to another user into an HTTP Request node and make genericAuthType (or the analogous nodeCredentialType) an expression that resolves to the real credential type only at execution time. CredentialsPermissionChecker statically computes active credential types from unresolved node parameters. Consequently any sender in a matched Teams route could reach conversationStore/dispatch and trigger a reply despite not being sender-allowlisted.

reasoning: The security invariant is that a checked pathname and the pathname dereferenced for a write must resolve to the same in-scope destination. The BIC's fallback checks a different object: after EvalSymlinks reports the dangling final link's missing destination, it discards the link component and validates only the lexical parent. causal_chain.bug_semantics: ScopedFs is intended to confine a user to a base directory. For an in-scope symlink whose out-of-scope final target does not yet exist, filepath.EvalSymlinks(target) returns fs.ErrNotExist. The vulnerable within()/WithinScope loop then replaces the link path with its lexical parent, resolves that in-scope directory, and returns true. guard() therefore permits OpenFile, while the subsequent base OpenFile with os.O_CREATE|os.O_TRUNC follows the symlink at the OS layer and creates attacker-controlled content outside the scope. An authenticated HTTP user with Create and Modify can reach this through POST /api/resources/<link>?override=true (and equivalent write paths). Existing out-of-scope targets are rejected; the escape is specific to a dangling target. The advisory declares github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/v2 <=2.63.15 affected and 2.63.16 first patched.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Incomplete symlink-confinement remediation in 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b. That one-parent commit first adds files.WithinScope and the faulty fs.ErrNotExist nearest-existing-ancestor loop to files/file.go, calls it from http/resource.go before OpenFile, and even documents that a dangling symlink is allowed because its containing directory is validated. Its direct parent 0231b7ebdfbe77a6c54027d30c4856c3fd81ee4d has neither WithinScope nor that fallback. Commit 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 later moves the same loop into new files/scoped.go as ScopedFs.within and is a carrier/refactor, not the first writer. The BIC first ships in v2.63.6; the residual remains in the predecessor issue's nominally patched v2.63.14 and in v2.63.15. Earlier releases had the broader unguarded symlink behavior, which explains the advisory's inclusive <=2.63.15 range; this BIC identifies the first writer of the residual patch-gap logic audited here.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.Reset() cleared output, global, culture, and source-file state but left the per-context CachedTemplates dictionary intact. IncludeFunction.Invoke() resolves an include through TemplateContext.GetOrCreateTemplate(); a cache hit returns the previously compiled Template without calling ITemplateLoader.Load(). An application that pools or reuses a TemplateContext across requests, users, or tenants can therefore prime an include under one authorization context and, after Reset(), expose that stale include content to a later context.

The vulnerability begins with this Reset contract, not with the older intentional within-context include cache; the commit is neither a move, refactor, revert, merge, nor squash aggregate.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.GetMemberAccessor cached one accessor per runtime Type, while TypedObjectAccessor captured the context's then-current MemberFilter and eagerly precomputed the exposed field/property set. After a permissive render populated that cache, resetting and reusing the same TemplateContext under a tighter MemberFilter returned the stale permissive accessor. ScriptMemberExpression therefore continued to read, and potentially write, members that the later sandbox policy denied, enabling cross-request or cross-tenant policy bypass when contexts were reused.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d added TemplateContext.MemberFilter and threaded it into the precomputed TypedObjectAccessor without changing the existing Dictionary<Type, IObjectAccessor> cache key or invalidation behavior. That commit is the first one in which a Type-only cached accessor can embody a context-specific filter policy.

With the default ObjectRecursionLimit of 0 (unlimited), a ScriptObject that directly or indirectly contains itself repeatedly re-enters ObjectToString until the CLR throws an uncatchable StackOverflowException, terminating the host process and enabling denial of service wherever an attacker can influence the rendered object graph.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated remote caller controls baseUrl in POST /api/provider-nodes/validate. The route passes baseUrl-derived URLs to server-side fetches and forwards the caller's apiKey as Authorization credentials. assertPublicUrl parses the URL, but its IPv4-mapped IPv6 check expects a dotted quad after ::ffff:, whereas WHATWG URL parsing canonicalizes that input to hexadecimal hextets first. Thus mapped loopback and link-local literals such as http://[::ffff:7f00:1] and http://[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe] pass the guard and reach internal services. The custom-embedding path reflects the first 200 response bytes for non-2xx responses other than 401/403; the other paths expose blind status/timing/port-scan signals. /api/provider-nodes is protected by dashboard authentication by default, but dashboardGuard permits access when requireLogin=false.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The lifecycle has distinct stages. 0a28f9f924d2dc53027a910679ee3cff3e63a59c created the caller-controlled provider validation fetch; 0b8bed5793c7a7c9beb7a5db7368720907f61ebc added the custom-embedding response-reflection amplifier; 090886ced9a3481837f5687ec66da7d9f33eea08 applied assertPublicUrl to remote requests. The smallest commit that first wrote the advisory's specifically flawed mapped-address defense is 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5: it added only the dotted-quad /^::ffff:(\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)$/ match and delegation to isBlockedIpv4. Its direct parent has the guard and sink but no mapped-address branch. The exploit therefore predates this attempted fix, while the defective defense itself originates in 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A browser page on an attacker-controlled DNS name can rebind that same origin to the victim's loopback Paperclip server. Because Paperclip did not reject the attacker's Host header and the default local-trusted behavior treated requests without credentials as an instance-admin board actor, the page could create a company and a process-adapter agent with attacker-controlled command/args, then invoke the agent heartbeat/wakeup route; the server passed that configuration to child_process.spawn as the Paperclip OS user, yielding drive-by command execution.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: abadd469bc85e9fa5137ff5ffce433f1c2db2c0b is the first commit that completed the exploitable mechanism: it mounted an actor middleware which assigned every unauthenticated request a board actor, added board-accessible company/agent creation and heartbeat invocation routes, and added the process execution service that spawned attacker-controlled command and args, all without Host validation. The parent had only CRUD agent routes and no auth middleware, heartbeat service, invocation route, or command sink. e1f2be7ecff711f2f5db9a0f64dbd3133df4410e later named/defaulted the same implicit-admin behavior as local_trusted; 85c0b9a3dc3795bf33646ef128ad070181c7abec later added a hostname guard but enabled it only for authenticated/private deployments, preserving the already-existing local-trusted flaw rather than introducing it.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The API scope middleware derives write versus read permission solely from the HTTP method and therefore treats every GET as read-only. The GET runner registration-token handlers are not read-only: shared.GetRegistrationToken calls NewRunnerToken when no active token exists and returns the usable token. A leaked read:user token (or the corresponding read-scoped owner/repository token) can consequently mint or obtain a runner registration credential, register an attacker-controlled Actions runner, and receive workflow work exposing source and repository secrets.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A scoped access token carrying only profile:read is accepted by PUT /user because that state-changing route is guarded with RequireScopes(ScopeProfileRead). UpdateUser derives the target from the token viewer, checks only that the target user is an administrator, and permits a supplied password to replace the administrator password. The attacker can then log in with that password; login issues a session-typed JWT, and RequireScopes deliberately bypasses all scope checks for session tokens, yielding an unrestricted administrator session.

The 2024 table-property rewrite did not create the flaw, and the 2026 helper commit is the direct closing fix. The BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit, so no squash decomposition is needed. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Second-order Oracle SQL identifier injection in the post-CREATE/post-UPDATE row lookup. Oracle table names are read verbatim from user_tables.TABLE_NAME and carried into the external-table query metadata. When Oracle returns response.lastRowid, OracleIntegration.query constructs SELECT * FROM "<table name>" WHERE ROWID = '<driver-produced ROWID>' by direct interpolation. An embedded double quote in the table name terminates the quoted identifier and makes the remainder SQL syntax. A user able to write that external table can trigger the lookup; the injected SQL runs with the configured Oracle datasource user's privileges and can cross Budibase's table/row authorization boundary. response.lastRowid is not the attacker-controlled part.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 is the smallest real origin: it replaced the prior returning implementation with a post-write ROWID lookup and first wrote the raw quoted-identifier interpolation, initially using json.endpoint.entityId. At that revision ExternalRequest derives endpoint.entityId directly from tableName, while Oracle schema introspection stores row.TABLE_NAME verbatim, so the original line already has the same identifier-injection semantics. dbe9eedcbadc6d164447078039801a53a2dcfa65 later changed the expression from json.endpoint.entityId to json.table.name but preserved the unsafe double-quote interpolation; it is a source-name rewrite, not the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Ech0 installed internal/i18n.Middleware() on the global Gin router, so every unauthenticated request supplied its raw, trimmed Accept-Language header to NewLocalizer. NewLocalizer passed that unbounded value directly to go-i18n, whose tag parsing reaches golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage. The x/text CVE-2022-32149 guard counts '-' separators but the scanner also aliases '_' to '-', so a near-1 MiB header made from malformed underscore-separated subtags bypasses the guard and exercises quadratic gobble/memmove behavior. The same unbounded parser was also reachable through X-Locale and the lang query parameter via ResolveLocale, with those explicit-locale paths potentially adding another parse. This is an unauthenticated CPU denial of service on public routes.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Application-boundary flaw first created by b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516: that single ordinary commit added the i18n implementation, directly forwarded acceptLanguage to goi18n.NewLocalizer, read Accept-Language from the request without a size/shape bound, and globally registered the middleware. The underlying parser behavior pre-existed in dependencies, but Ech0's remotely reachable unbounded data path did not exist in the immediate parent.

Run `git show --format=fuller --stat --patch b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go internal/router/middleware.go go.mod go.sum` in the validated clone. The commit creates internal/i18n/i18n.go; ResolveLocale passes joined raw values to language.ParseAcceptLanguage, NewLocalizer returns goi18n.NewLocalizer(bundle, locale, acceptLanguage), Middleware reads strings.TrimSpace(ctx.GetHeader("Accept-Language")), and internal/router/middleware.go adds r.Use(i18nUtil.Middleware()). It also first adds go-i18n v2.6.1 to go.mod.

The independent history cross-checks converge on the same BIC. `git log -L ':Middleware:internal/i18n/i18n.go' main` reaches the /dev/null addition in b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516; `git log -L ':NewLocalizer:internal/i18n/i18n.go' main` shows the unfiltered sink added by that commit and changed only by the fix. Pickaxe commands `git log --all -S'ctx.GetHeader("Accept-Language")' -- internal/i18n/i18n.go`, `git log --all -S'return goi18n.NewLocalizer(bundle, locale, acceptLanguage)' -- internal/i18n/i18n.go`, and `git log --all -S'r.Use(i18nUtil.Middleware())' -- internal/router/middleware.go` all identify b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 as the first addition on the application history; later dc03197eeb4b5f28ebe794f45732cd4d04d53b1c refactors the middleware but preserves the unbounded sink.

Direct parent verification: `git ls-tree -r --name-only b00c0f7da80cdbf4f4bd84a0c557ae03c88775a6 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go internal/router/middleware.go go.mod` lists only go.mod and internal/router/middleware.go, not internal/i18n/i18n.go. `git show b00c0f7da80cdbf4f4bd84a0c557ae03c88775a6:internal/router/middleware.go` contains Recovery, Cors, and WriteGuard only, with no i18n registration; searching that parent's go.mod for go-i18n produces no match. Thus the immediate parent lacks both the vulnerable parser path and its global exposure.

`git cat-file -p b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516` gives exactly one parent, b00c0f7da80cdbf4f4bd84a0c557ae03c88775a6, and a direct tree diff. It is not a merge, release, move, revert, or publicly decomposable squash aggregate, so the ordinary commit itself is the smallest public-history BIC and decomposed_shas is empty.

Introduction boundary: `git show -s --format='%H %ad %s' v4.0.0^{}` resolves v4.0.0 to 93b935c5b64020c7475abb9df071fdf8663b9f84, and `git ls-tree -r --name-only v4.0.0 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go` has no output. v4.1.0 resolves to d1f0768e8d469179d5ee8634c2c3311ed31e1d26; `git grep -n -E 'Accept-Language|NewLocalizer\(bundle|i18nUtil.Middleware' v4.1.0 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go internal/router/middleware.go` shows the raw header, unfiltered NewLocalizer sink, and global middleware registration. Closing fix: `git show --format=fuller --patch a5e77c4af60ead1cad3b3e8e0a3ed6f30892ed09 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go internal/i18n/i18n_test.go` shows commit a5e77c4af60ead1cad3b3e8e0a3ed6f30892ed09 adding maxAcceptLanguageSeparators=32 and sanitizeAcceptLanguage, applying it to every ResolveLocale part and immediately before goi18n.NewLocalizer. This directly closes the Accept-Language, X-Locale, lang-query, and later-caller sinks; its sole parent is ccfb304534d8f1260611bb4af3d3f3ab69ac00ed.

Fix release boundary: v5.0.0 resolves to 4deb936608843fab40692788cf299700bb6637bf and `git grep -n -E 'Accept-Language|sanitizeAcceptLanguage|NewLocalizer\(bundle' v5.0.0 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go` shows the raw header and unfiltered goi18n.NewLocalizer call with no sanitizer. `git tag --contains a5e77c4af60ead1cad3b3e8e0a3ed6f30892ed09 --sort=version:refname` first lists v5.0.2/ech0-5.0.2 among normal version tags; v5.0.2 resolves to release commit f715214732db93067718150cb3b2bad8fe9be827, and the same grep at v5.0.2 shows sanitizer calls. The validated clone has no v5.0.1 tag, so v5.0.2 is the first repository-verifiable fixed tag even though the first-party advisory declares 5.0.1+ patched.

reasoning: The security invariant is per-path rule enforcement, but the mutation handlers authorized only roots and then delegated recursive filesystem work with no checker. f6816c9a is the smallest persistent first-writer for the earliest affected operation, and its immediate parent lacks that resource delete path; later rename and copy commits extend the same flaw, while the 2019 v2 rewrite and 2021 root-check patch are not origins. The direct fix pre-walks every source descendant and its projected destination and rejects the mutation if any rule denies a path, closing all three vectors in v2.63.22. Because the BIC is a 2017 human-authored commit whose raw commit object has no AI marker, the causal verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: File Browser applies path rules to only the requested source root (and, for copy/rename, the destination root), then recursively copies, renames, or removes the entire source tree without checking each descendant. An authenticated restricted user can therefore operate on an allowed parent containing a denied child: copy or rename makes the denied child accessible at an allowed destination, while delete destroys it.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The earliest persistent resource-API vector is f6816c9a39702484ad7c5c3672209bbc4ce5f948: serveAPI checks c.us.Allowed(r.URL.Path) once, then the newly added deleteHandler calls fileSystem.RemoveAll recursively. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated users remain inside their configured filesystem scope but can bypass administrator path deny rules because authorization compares the uncanonicalized virtual path literally while the backing filesystem resolves an equivalent name differently. On Windows, a mixed-separator traversal such as /allow\..\Secret.txt likewise misses the slash-based rule while filepath/afero resolves it to the denied file. The affected operations include reads and, subject to the user's ordinary permissions, modification, deletion, copying, and sharing; internally generated OS-separated paths also caused nested recursive/archive checks to miss rules on Windows.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated TUS PATCH endpoint appended the entire request body with io.Copy even after the server had parsed and cached the Upload-Length declared at upload creation. The cached length was consulted only after the write to decide that an upload was complete. A create-capable user could therefore declare a 1 KiB upload and stream an arbitrarily large PATCH body, which was fully written before HTTP 204, allowing disk exhaustion. The fix bounds each write to Upload-Length minus Upload-Offset, rejects an already-excessive offset, and truncates and returns 413 when the body is over-length.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest causal commit is PR #5270 member 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5, not its later GitHub squash 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e and not the 2023 commit that originally added io.Copy. Member 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5 first parsed Upload-Length, registered that accepted length, retrieved it in PATCH, and compared newOffset against it only after the pre-existing unbounded copy. Before that member, the endpoint had an unbounded upload operation but no accepted/cached per-upload declared bound; consistent with the first-party advisory's out-of-scope distinction for uploads without such a bound, that older behavior is not this specific bypass.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In filebrowser v2, an authenticated user confined to an otherwise-authorized scope but configured with Perm.Download=false can send GET /api/resources/<same-scope-file>?checksum=md5|sha1|sha256|sha512. resourceGetHandler invokes FileInfo.Checksum, which reads the file, and renderJSON returns the digest without checking Download. This bypasses only the Download permission, not scope/path authorization: it exposes a content-hash oracle usable for known-content confirmation, change detection, or offline guessing of low-entropy content, and forces a full-file read. The vulnerable v2 implementation is present from v2.0.0-rc.1 (and stable v2.0.0) through v2.63.18; v2.63.19 closes it.

reasoning: The report's proposed attack crosses the browser/server boundary: changing a browser request is always possible, so a bypass exists only if the Frontend API fails to bind an OTP attempt to the prepared factor and sign-in state. The public SDK at 5.88.0 passes the UI-selected factor strategy and code to that API, but contains no server-side authentication decision. Git diff shows 5.88.0 did not introduce the relevant request path, and git log -L shows the generic path existed years earlier. There is no closing patch or first patched package version; 5.89.0's OTP work only changes the input UI. Most decisively, on 2025-12-23 the CNA withdrew the CVE after determining it was not a security issue, and Clerk's first-party history says it was never a real vulnerability. Selecting the 2022 request helper, the 5.88.0 release commit, or any later change as a BIC would therefore violate the protocol's requirement for the smallest commit that first wrote genuinely vulnerable lines. Since no true BIC exists, there is no parent-absence claim and no BIC commit object on which an AI marker may be judged. EVIDENCE_GAP is used rather than NOT_AI because a closed NOT_AI verdict requires a real BIC; it is used rather than BLOCKED because the repository and public lifecycle are accessible, but the reachable evidence does not establish any vulnerability to attribute.

The public clerk-js 5.88.0 UI does send the factor strategy and entered code to the Frontend API, but that client-controlled request is not an authentication trust boundary; the alleged bypass requires the server to accept a strategy that was not valid for the sign-in attempt. The CNA later rejected CVE-2025-63700 because further investigation established that this was not a security issue.

Commit b233f27910f32c264243d03021e4f25dbef5f403 is therefore the first complete vulnerable tree: it deliberately publishes the dormant unsafe handler to authenticated users, and its immediate parent lacks that route. This is smaller and causally later than the 2024 aggregate that wrote the dormant method, so no squash decomposition is applicable to the selected BIC. The direct fix 4a52477e6ed66afa436814c80e7bcd68670dd596 closes both tenant selection and mass-assignment paths and strengthens action authorization, with the internal version boundary 5.3.1 to 5.3.2 and tagged v5.5.3 containing it. causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated attacker can send PUT /api/supplier/{victim_id}. The route has only auth:api middleware and SupplierRequest::authorize() merely checks Auth::check(); SupplierUpdateController then resolves the identifier globally with Supplier::find($id), updates it from $request->all(), and returns the resulting supplier. Because Supplier::$fillable includes company_id while the request rules do not constrain that field and sensitive supplier fields are not hidden, the attacker can read and modify another tenant's supplier and reassign it by supplying company_id.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The unsafe SupplierUpdateController method body was present but dormant from b03c8c6f5fde097cbe44552464c56469b60a4369 (APP_VERSION 4.0.0): neither that revision nor tagged v2.0.1/v4.6.0 registered a supplier PUT API route. The smallest commit that completed the externally reachable vulnerable mechanism was b233f27910f32c264243d03021e4f25dbef5f403, which imported SupplierUpdateController and added the auth-only PUT /supplier/{id} route while leaving the pre-existing unscoped lookup and mass assignment intact; it set APP_VERSION to 4.15.0.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored graph-configuration XSS. An authenticated low-privilege user could POST a config_json object containing a style such as mispStyles.Event.svgIcon. The save route checked only that the string parsed as JSON and persisted the complete object; the list route returned the stored string unchanged. When a viewer with access to the saved row (notably an administrator, because administrators list every user's configs) loaded it, graphConfigModal.js parsed config_json and applyConfig() spread every property of each stixStyles/mispStyles entry into GRAPH_CONFIG. A subsequent graph render passed that style map to Pivotick as nodeStyleMap. The bundled Pivotick renderer treats svgIcon as markup (both a template path using template.innerHTML = i.svgIcon.trim() and node rendering using an SVG element's innerHTML), so a crafted SVG event handler executes in the viewer's browser. Loading/applying the saved configuration is the victim interaction.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a is the atomic first writer of the vulnerable cross-user path. It added the GraphConfig table/model, /graph_config/save and /graph_config/list, the saved-config modal/load code, and applyConfig(), whose unrestricted object spread copied attacker-controlled style members such as svgIcon into GRAPH_CONFIG. The pre-existing parent already rendered trusted built-in styles with Pivotick, but had no saved-config file, persistence route, load path, or applyConfig bridge from another user's stored JSON to that renderer.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated cross-tenant IDOR/BOLA in the web ticket CRUD: GET /ticket/update/{id} loaded Ticket::find($id) and exposed another tenant's ticket content and attachments; POST /ticket/save accepted an attacker-selected ticket id, loaded that record without company_id scoping, then overwrote company_id with the attacker's company and saved it; GET /ticket/delete/{id} loaded and deleted any numeric ticket id without tenant scoping, and its generic Request parameter bypassed the authorization implemented by TicketDeleteRequest.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The original ticket CRUD commit 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd directly introduced the first vulnerable read and save endpoints and their unscoped Ticket::find lookups. causal_chain.bug_semantics: POST /company/save accepted a company logo without server-side type, extension, size, or SVG-content validation. An authenticated user satisfying the route's create company and update company permission gates could upload an SVG containing an embedded script; the controller derived a .svg destination name and wrote it to public storage. The resulting /storage/company/{slug}/{file} resource was served statically outside Laravel authentication, so direct navigation by any visitor executed attacker-controlled JavaScript in the application origin.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c is the smallest true BIC: it first added the logo multipart field (explicitly accepting image/svg), copied an uploaded logo under the public webroot using the content-derived extension, and performed no validation. Later controller extraction, formatting, repository refactoring, and the 2026 public-disk rewrite preserved the same unrestricted-upload decision rather than introducing it.

It also states that every existing tag is vulnerable and that the fix is not tagged.

In the validated clone, `git show --format=fuller --patch dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c` shows the BIC adding `request->file('logo')->extension()`, copying the upload to `public/asset/upload/company/{slug}/{timestamp}.{extension}`, saving the filename, and adding a multipart file input whose accept list includes image/svg. `git log --all -S"request->file('logo')" -- app/Http/Controllers` returns dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c as the first writer.

Direct parent verification is reproducible with `git show 4f6c90f21a3b1c826f65d554572c87647994e055:app/Http/Controllers/CompanyController.php`: save() only copies scalar company fields and has no logo field, file access, extension derivation, public write, or equivalent upload path. `git cat-file -p dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c` confirms that exact commit's sole parent is 4f6c90f21a3b1c826f65d554572c87647994e055.

Thus neither the move nor later rewrite is the BIC.

At vulnerable parent 54713abef6a89fdd3d9534c06f232dcecae4f6ca, `routes/module/company.php` chains `can('create company')` and `can('update company')` on POST /company/save; CompanySaveController also checks create versus update authorization and company ownership. Its upload block calls `storeAs($folder, $filename, 'public')` with no validation. `config/filesystems.php` maps the public disk to storage/app/public, URL APP_URL/storage, and public/storage symlink; the logo views use /storage/company/{slug}/{logo}.

`git show --format=fuller --patch aaa4fc76bf039d5011884b86b8f29ddd50d17b17` shows the direct one-parent fix replacing the raw Request with CompanySaveRequest, validating logo MIME/size, and applying ValidateSafeSvg, which rejects script tags, event handlers, javascript: URLs, iframe, object, and embed content before storage. reasoning: The vulnerability begins when the authenticated save route first accepts a caller-controlled existing contact id and resolves it without deriving or checking tenant ownership. That happened in 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9; although contacts did not yet have a direct company_id column, they belonged to tenant-owned leads/customers, so arbitrary-id overwrite was already cross-tenant. The later 65f6b9f9 repository commit preserves and relocates the same lookup, so treating it as the introducer would violate the protocol's no-move/no-refactor rule. Later commits expand the same authorization failure to vCard export and supplier contacts but do not move the lifecycle's earliest boundary. The direct fix consistently binds every affected lookup to the authenticated company, and the immediately following version bump establishes 5.4.8 as the first fixed version. Because the actual BIC commit object has a human identity and no AI marker, later AI evidence on the 2026 fix/version commits is out of scope; the required BIC-only classification is NOT_AI.

Equivalent supplier-contact save and export paths had the same missing company_id constraint.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: rConfig deliberately disabled self-registration with Auth::routes(['register' => false]), but a later bare Auth::routes() registered Laravel's default POST /register route again. An unauthenticated request could therefore reach RegisterController, whose create() inserted name, email, and password without a role; the users.role database default was Admin. The framework registration trait then authenticated the newly created full-Administrator account, exposing device credentials, users, and API-token functionality without invitation, approval, or email verification.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated path traversal and arbitrary file read in GET /download-export. routes/web.php places the endpoint inside the auth middleware group, but FileDownloadController::download_export() formed $path as export_path() . $_GET['filename']; file_exists() was the only gate before response()->download($path). A low-privilege authenticated caller could therefore supply ../ segments (for example, ../../.env relative to storage/app/rconfig/exports/) to escape the exports directory and download any file readable by the web-server process, exposing secrets such as application keys and database or mail credentials.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8 is the atomic first writer of the flawed sink: it created app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php with download_export(), the raw $_GET['filename'] concatenation, the file_exists() check, and response()->download(), and added export_path(). Its direct parent 09fa5a4eac1abb8ee5010bb85b39411f36a6fa5e has no FileDownloadController, no export_path() helper, and no download-export route; only DeviceInventoryExporter already emitted a link to that not-yet-routed endpoint. causal_chain.bug_semantics: awxkit's custom PyYAML Loader registers !include and !import and passes attacker-controlled scalar, sequence, or mapping values to extractFile(). Before the fix, extractFile() joined that value to the importing YAML file's directory, expanded it with glob.glob(), converted matches to absolute paths, and opened them without rejecting absolute paths, '..' traversal, or symlink escapes. A user who runs 'awx --conf.format yaml import' on a crafted YAML document can therefore cause the local client to read and parse arbitrary YAML-formatted files outside the document directory. The attack is local/client-side, requires the victim to import the malicious file, and compromises confidentiality.

The source authoring history is not present in the validated clone or exposed by the import PR, so the true BIC cannot be named without substituting an excluded aggregate import.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /tokenTransfer/:token handler treats knowledge of a random transfer UUID as sufficient authority. POST stores the originating author's token and createdAt under that UUID, but GET neither checks createdAt nor removes the record, so a leaked URL remains redeemable indefinitely and repeatedly. GET also serializes the stored record, including the raw author token, in its response body, defeating the HttpOnly boundary and enabling persistent authorship impersonation. The attacker needs a legitimate user to create a transfer and must obtain its UUID out of band, but needs no Etherpad authentication to redeem it.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: On Linux/Unix, an attacker-controlled RAR entry such as `..\..\tmp\evil.txt` is first checked as a child of the extraction directory while backslashes are literal filename characters, so `getCanonicalPath().startsWith(destination.getCanonicalPath())` accepts it. `makeFile()` then splits that same name on backslashes, joins the components with the platform `File.separator` (`/`), creates the resulting directories/file, and `extract()` writes attacker-controlled entry bytes through `FileOutputStream`. The validation and the write therefore interpret the same pathname differently, enabling traversal and arbitrary file overwrite outside the destination. Windows is not affected by this bypass because canonicalization already treats backslashes as separators.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The earliest public Git commit, root commit 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519 (`initial import`), first writes the operative vulnerable extraction logic in `testutil/src/main/java/de/innosystec/unrar/testutil/ExtractArchive.java`: it splits entry names on backslashes, rebuilds them with `File.separator`, and opens the result for output. Subsequent commits only relocate or copy that logic: 7e0c503f3afe6da766e4476333bc3ee9cd677bb1 renames the package, e5b90d174c5a426a134b00a33ddece3ac9e82a39 moves it into the main unrar module, bb362df3e1e5471e58f6322c91b7b1c9a8ebaef1 moves the module tree, 75cb6a58c9b3ca08db954eec241b91a5331dd632 copies it into `Junrar`, and 3b645d991563dd8933f6efab135cd76a43a92d6b copies it into `LocalFolderExtractor`. Commit e60b915f8932c08b9b6874a97f00676decba069a later added canonical-path validation but left the backslash-to-platform-separator conversion after the check, so it failed to close the original Unix traversal.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The soffice-backed import/export paths placed working files in the shared directory returned by os.tmpdir() under names derived from non-cryptographic Math.random(), without exclusive creation or no-follow protection. A local user able to predict or race a token could pre-create a symlink at an export source path (or a converter destination path); ExportHandler's fs.writeFile then followed the link and truncated/wrote the linked target with exported HTML, subject to the Etherpad process's filesystem privileges. The import conversion destination was likewise predictable and could receive partially attacker-controlled converted upload content. Shared-host local access and a target writable by Etherpad are required.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The Admin Console gadget endpoint embeds the request parameter in gf.getGadgetModule("#{param.gadget}", ...). JSFTemplating Handler.getInputValue resolves that outer expression through ComponentUtil.resolveValue; after param.gadget becomes an attacker string, resolveValue treats a resulting #{...} string as another ValueExpression and evaluates it. Thus a request to the gadget.jsf XML-loader endpoint can make attacker-supplied EL execute server-side before the resulting value is treated as the gadget path/URL. The vulnerable EL resolver allowed class/getClass, static method, constructor, and static-field access, turning the double evaluation into RCE; a cross-site request supplies the UI interaction reflected by CVSS UI:R.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated GlassFish Administration Console uses JSFTemplating as its view-description/templating engine. JSFTemplating accepted and evaluated EL from console request processing with the ordinary Faces ELContext and no resolver in front of the standard resolver chain to reject dangerous reflective/static constructs. A crafted authenticated panel request could therefore reach static methods or constructors, getClass()/class traversal, and static fields; an attacker could reach Java process-execution facilities and run operating-system commands as the GlassFish service account. The closing component change installs RestrictedELResolver ahead of PageSessionResolver and rejects ELClass method invocation/constructors, getClass(), the class property, and (in the immediately following hardening commit) static fields.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The unsafe EL design predates the available Git history. In eclipse-ee4j/glassfish-jsftemplating, blame of VariableResolver.java attributes the request-parameter datasource, method-expression creation, and general variable-resolution machinery to root commit 18d9b835fa98caec01ef026aab5ed907567dec0d, an 'Initial Contribution' importing 300 files and 141,910 lines whose source headers date the implementation to 2006. In eclipse-ee4j/glassfish, root commit 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb is likewise an aggregate 'Initial Contribution' and already pins vulnerable jsftemplating 2.1.3. Neither aggregate is the smallest commit that originally wrote the flaw, and neither has a parent/history from which that commit can be decomposed.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: With the admin API enabled, a database-backed principal holding gateways.read can submit an attacker-controlled hostname to POST /admin/gateways/test. Validation resolves that hostname and rejects private, loopback, link-local, reserved, and metadata addresses, but the accepted URL retains the hostname. ResilientHttpClient/httpx then resolves the hostname again when connecting. An attacker-controlled DNS server can therefore return a public address for the validation lookup and a private or metadata address for the connection lookup, bypassing the SSRF checks and returning internal response content.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The exact check/use race first appears in PR #3115 member d34f611030166bbdd4ea2d93d909098c9dc8d934: it inserted SecurityValidator.validate_url() before the existing gateway-test request, while leaving the outbound request addressed by the validated hostname rather than the checked IP. PR #3115 was squash-landed on the release line as d549137791f10c59c00ec3e89cb55cd560a8248f. Later hardening 2b5b9e9a145304c466966c560e82d4682849b13a added an allowlist and an explicit ICACF-15 rebinding TODO, and fb4d9a2616f22dcc64239b250b1c6389b638de4f consolidated validation into validate_gateway_test_url(), but both retained independent connection-time DNS resolution. The race was closed by fba11a99babd80779fa05510b35fb6a153bbacaf, which captures a safe resolved IP, rewrites the dial target to that IP, preserves the original Host authority and TLS SNI, and was released in v1.0.3.

The public PR commit list at https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/pull/3115/commits enumerates seven member commits and identifies d34f611030166bbdd4ea2d93d909098c9dc8d934 as `fix: outbound url validation hardening and behavior consistency`, with body text `validate admin gateway test base URL before outbound requests`; the squash commit d549137791f10c59c00ec3e89cb55cd560a8248f includes that member subject and content.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: DownloadFileRequestHandler derives fileName from the /file/* path, then accepts the request's version parameter and passes it unchanged to BaseUtils.replaceFileNameAndExtension. That helper returns FilenameUtils.getFullPath(fileName) + version, and FileUtils.readFile/createFile ultimately opens new File(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName) without canonical containment checking. On the unauthenticated /file/static/noauth/** route, a request to /file/static/noauth with a version such as ../../... therefore replaces the benign basename with a traversal path and reads a server file outside the download folder.

The shared ZipUtils implementation ultimately exposed the same sink to both EmailReceiver and MakeUnzipFileAction.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated federated ActivityPub server can send a Create/Note whose sanitized content contains an emoji shortcode and whose attacker-controlled Emoji tag supplies icon.url and name. NodeBB replaces the shortcode after the content sanitization pass with an HTML img string containing those values in quoted attributes, then stores that generated HTML. The remote-post display path can return the stored HTML without a subsequent markdown/sanitize-html pass, so an attribute-breaking value becomes persistent same-origin XSS for viewers. The first exploitable sink interpolated icon.url; commit 3968c822a2291d32d79a86ba625858a90e8496f9 subsequently added the unescaped title from tag.name.

Its parent has no emoji rewrite or tag.icon.url use in that file. causal_chain.bug_semantics: @cleverbrush/deep deepExtend recursively copies every enumerable source key into a fresh ordinary object without rejecting __proto__. From ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6 onward, the merge loop uses Reflect.has(o1, key). For attacker-controlled JSON containing an own __proto__ object, Reflect.has sees the inherited __proto__ accessor on an ordinary target; o1[key] resolves to Object.prototype, both sides satisfy the object checks, and extendObject recurses into Object.prototype. Attacker-chosen inner properties are then assigned as own properties of Object.prototype and become inherited by every ordinary object in the realm. An application reaches the sink by passing parsed request/config/query data to deepExtend; the resulting realm-wide inherited values can corrupt authorization or configuration logic, cause denial of service, or feed a secondary gadget. The disclosed working route is __proto__; constructor is a function on the ordinary receiver and therefore does not take this recursion branch, although the closing defense rejects __proto__, constructor, and prototype.

That semantic change made inherited __proto__ appear to be an existing object and redirected recursion into Object.prototype. The absence of an unsafe-key denylist was older, but the immediate parent assigned __proto__ on the local merge receiver instead of recursively writing attacker properties into Object.prototype, so the realm-wide primitive reported in issue #213 begins at this commit. Later commits only reformatted, typed, or documented the same vulnerable loop until the fix.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated Project Managers or Owners can store an attacker-controlled repository git_url beginning with a Git option such as --upload-pack=... . With the default cmd_git client, the server-side schedule commit-hash poller passes that value to git ls-remote before the repository operand and without --end-of-options. Git interprets it as an option and invokes the supplied upload-pack command through a shell, yielding command execution in the Semaphore server process. Repository validation checked only that GitURL was nonempty while branch validation did not delimit the URL argument.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The exploitable schedule-poller data flow was introduced by a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f (fix(be): bug with getting remote commit), which changed GetLastRemoteCommitHash from git ls-remote origin <branch> in a repository directory to git ls-remote <Repository.GetGitURL()> <branch> in the temporary directory. This was the first write that put attacker-controlled GitURL into the ls-remote option-parsing position; later file moves and client refactors only preserved it.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An initialized XKB client can send two SetMap requests with XkbSetMapResizeTypes. That writes mapWidths[255..264], nine bytes beyond the fixed stack array in _XkbSetMapChecks and into adjacent stack state, enabling server crash and potentially privilege escalation when the X server is privileged.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A caller able to reach GET /api could supply an arbitrary http(s) url. The route passed that value into extractWeb, whose timeout wrapper called the server's fetch implementation directly, with no destination-address validation and ordinary redirect behavior. PullMD could therefore request loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, or cloud-metadata resources from its own network position and return the retrieved content as Markdown; the reported concrete payload targeted Alibaba-style metadata at http://100.100.100.200/latest/user-data. The same unguarded extraction primitive was also reachable from MCP read_url and stale-share refresh paths.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Public-history root commit 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d, 'Initial public release', created server.js with app.get('/api') forwarding req.query.url to extractWebFn and created lib/web.js with extractWeb wrapping globalThis.fetch and executing await fetchFn(url, { headers }) without any scheme, DNS, address-range, or redirect-hop guard. It also created the MCP read_url caller. This is the first and smallest Git commit object that writes the vulnerable route/sink in the available repository: git -L and -S both terminate at that root, and the root has no parent object to contain the lines. It is not a later move, refactor, revert, release carrier, or identifiable squash carrier; there are no member commits in the available history to decompose.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When AUTH_ENABLED=true, is_internal_request() checks an external request's optional X-Internal-Service header against the defaultless INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET with direct equality. If the environment variable is unset and the attacker omits the header, both lookups return None, so None == None is true. verify_api_key() then returns the trusted internal principal with scopes ["all"] before requiring an API key; that scope satisfies require_scope("admin") and permits unauthenticated creation (including admin-scoped keys), enumeration, and revocation of API keys. The /admin/generate-master-key route is not itself reachable through this bypass because it additionally requires is_master_key=true, contrary to that part of the issue/advisory impact wording.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: CWE-918 SSRF: an unauthenticated proxy caller could supply x-headroom-base-url and make Headroom issue the request to a caller-selected http(s) destination. The original catch-all route passed that value directly to handle_passthrough, which appended the inbound path, copied all inbound headers except Host (including Authorization), sent the request with httpx, and returned the upstream response. Later OpenAI and Azure/passthrough resolution paths preserved the same trust error. Without rejecting loopback, link-local, RFC1918, metadata, or other non-public addresses, a remotely exposed proxy could disclose internal-service responses and forward caller credentials to the chosen host.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f is the smallest first-writer. It added the x-headroom-base-url catch-all override in headroom/proxy/server.py and immediately passed custom_base.rstrip('/') to handle_passthrough without destination validation. The later b17c6d81cc39676f322779dc2e5695cba28b8e65 extraction into headroom/providers/proxy_routes.py, 7d747306066de6ed9f2635b58860f7d85fdf6362 compatibility work, and c19347c31046bf25baf9b1a816c9bede5d3ee807 OpenAI resolver are lifecycle moves/extensions, not the BIC.

reasoning: The causal boundary is the 2015 CPU-atlas optimization, not the original 2014 glamor text code: before 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f there was no heap backing buffer for per-glyph memcpy to overrun; that commit simultaneously introduced the maxbounds-sized heap allocation and unchecked per-glyph copy. Its immediate parent directly lacks both operations, and -L/-S history agrees. The 2026 mainline fix and its two release-branch backports close exactly that invariant violation and establish the published fixed versions. causal_chain.bug_semantics: In the Xorg DRI2 request path, a client controls the attachment list passed by ProcDRI2GetBuffers or ProcDRI2GetBuffersWithFormat to do_get_buffers. The vulnerable code allocates count + 1 DRI2BufferPtr slots but treats requested attachment multiplicity as arithmetic: every DRI2BufferBackLeft increments need_real_front, while one DRI2BufferFrontLeft decrements it only once and also increments need_fake_front for a window. With at least two BackLeft entries and one FrontLeft, both counters remain positive after the count input entries are stored, so the function appends both an implicit real-front and an implicit fake-front buffer. The fake-front pointer is written at buffers[count + 1], one element beyond the count + 1 allocation, causing a client-triggerable heap out-of-bounds write and permitting server crash or privilege escalation when the X server is privileged.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341 replaced the earlier bulk CreateBuffers path with the new per-attachment do_get_buffers implementation for DRI2GetBuffersWithFormat. In that same atomic change it introduced the undersized buffers = xalloc((count + 1) * sizeof(buffers[0])) allocation, the multiplicity-sensitive need_real_front/need_fake_front counters, and the two independent post-loop buffers[i++] appends. That newly created combination is the root cause; 4fad615d689c61c6c3a000295a1fa755359737cb is a later branch cherry-pick of the same patch, not the original BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An XKB-capable local client can use XkbSetMap to replace a non-canonical key type with wire numLevels=255. CheckKeyTypes accepted every positive CARD8 width and stored it without enforcing XkbMaxShiftLevel=63. A later core ChangeKeyboardMapping reaches XkbUpdateKeyTypesFromCore; XkbKeyTypesForCoreSymbols derives groupsWidth from the attacker-controlled num_levels and uses XKB_OFFSET(g,l)=(g*groupsWidth)+l against a stack KeySym tsyms[XkbMaxSymsPerKey] buffer of 252 entries. With four groups and width 255, indices reach 1019, 767 entries beyond the buffer; the related fixed-size symbol/action temporaries make this a set of stack-overflow paths capable of server crash and, for a root X server, privilege escalation.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A client able to change the X server font path can create a directory whose fonts.alias maps an alias to a 257-1023-byte target, add that directory with SetFontPath, and request the alias with ListFonts or ListFontsWithInfo. libXfont2 accepts and returns names/alias targets up to its 1024-byte MAXFONTNAMELEN, while the server historically used XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN=256 for the stack-local tmp_pattern and the LFWIstateRec current.pattern arrays. doListFontsAndAliases copied resolvedlen bytes into tmp_pattern and then current.pattern without checking resolvedlen; doListFontsWithInfo likewise copied namelen bytes into current.pattern without checking namelen. The oversized library-produced target therefore writes beyond stack buffers, permitting a server crash and potentially privilege escalation when the X server runs as root.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable 256-byte server buffers and all three relevant unchecked alias-resolution copies are already present in ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1, the 2003-11-14 whole-tree snapshot whose message is 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line'. That changeset creates dix/dixfonts.c and include/closestr.h wholesale on top of a parent containing neither path, so it is an aggregate import boundary rather than the smallest source commit and is rejected as the BIC. Later 05a793f5b3c40747d5a92a076def7f4fb673c7e7 merely migrated the pre-existing code from libXfont to libXfont2, and 5cc24dbb4c151023dc0d18e16001e27f87ae8391 merely changed non-overlapping memmove calls to memcpy; neither first introduced the unchecked length-versus-buffer mismatch. The true originating source change predates the fine-grained history available for these paths in this repository.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated POST parameter request at /cgi-bin/api.values.get is parsed character by character by the Grandstream firmware's 32-bit ARM /app/bin/gs_web service. Non-colon bytes are copied into a 64-byte stack buffer and a terminator is appended without checking that the current colon-delimited component is at most 63 bytes. An overlong component therefore overwrites the stack; repeated colon-delimited components permit multiple strategically placed NUL writes, enabling a ROP chain and unauthenticated command execution as root.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Grandstream GXP1600-series proprietary firmware, specifically the api.values.get handler in /app/bin/gs_web; rapid7/metasploit-framework contains the later exploit and post-exploitation modules, not the affected firmware implementation.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A remote discovery report can carry a 255-byte EIR/advertising-data block whose first name element has field_len 254, so eir_parse derives data_len 253 and passes it to name2utf8. name2utf8 copies len attacker-controlled bytes with strncpy into utf8_name[HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH + 2], only 250 bytes because HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH is 248. The resulting three-byte stack overwrite can crash bluetoothd and can also leave the local array unterminated for subsequent strtoutf8/g_strstrip/g_strdup reads, with potential code execution depending on the build and architecture.

Although the subject says 'Move', this is not a mere relocation of an already-vulnerable EIR sink: the parent has no name2utf8 in src/eir.c and rejects malformed EIR names; the copied event.c pattern used a fixed MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH count rather than the EIR element's variable len.

audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 changed EIR name handling from rejecting invalid UTF-8 and safely g_strndup-ing accepted data to routing it through a newly added name2utf8 function. That new EIR-specific function introduced the fixed 250-byte stack buffer and the attacker-sized strncpy without a length clamp. Although the subject says 'Move', this is not a mere relocation of an already-vulnerable EIR sink: the parent has no name2utf8 in src/eir.c and rejects malformed EIR names; the copied event.c pattern used a fixed MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH count rather than the EIR element's variable len.
audit_record.ai_marker: No AI marker. `git cat-file commit 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22` shows human author and committer Johan Hedberg <johan.hedberg@intel.com> and only the message `core: Move UTF-8 validation of device names into eir.c`; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: Upstream first-party advisory https://github.com/bluez/bluez/security/advisories/GHSA-68h6-5qgp-3975 identifies CVE-2026-80186, src/eir.c:name2utf8, a remotely supplied EIR name, field_len 254/data_len 253, the 250-byte stack buffer, affected version 5.86, and patched commit 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2.

At 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^, `git grep -n HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH -- lib/bluetooth/hci.h src/eir.c` shows HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH is 248 and name2utf8 declares `char utf8_name[HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH + 2]`; `git blame -L 136,150 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^ -- src/eir.c` attributes the buffer, memset, attacker-sized `strncpy(utf8_name, (char *) name, len)`, strip, and duplicate lines to 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22.

`git blame -L 250,306 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^ -- src/eir.c` reproduces the length path: uint8_t field_len, `len += field_len + 1`, only an aggregate `len > eir_len` rejection, `data_len = field_len - 1`, and name fields passed as `name2utf8(data, data_len)`. `git grep -n -C 25 'btd_adapter_device_found(adapter, &ev->addr.bdaddr' 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^ -- src/adapter.c` shows the remote MGMT Device Found event supplies its eir/eir_len to the discovery path, and the callee's data_len is uint8_t, permitting 255.

`git log 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^ -L ':name2utf8:src/eir.c'` and `git log master --reverse -S 'strncpy(utf8_name, (char *) name, len)' -- src/eir.c` both reach 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 as the first writer of the vulnerable EIR sink; the later 218db700f49370bc07ce1e6d609d28d846470d99 only removes the valid-UTF-8 fast path and changes conversion, while the unsafe buffer and variable-length copy remain attributed to 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22.

`git show --find-renames --find-copies 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22` shows the newly added name2utf8 and the name-case call replacing the parent's validation/g_strndup path. `git rev-parse 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22^` returns 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e; `git grep -n -e name2utf8 -e 'strncpy(utf8_name, (char *) name, len)' 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e -- src/eir.c` has no match, while `git grep -n -C 6 g_utf8_validate 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e -- src/eir.c` shows malformed names were rejected and accepted names used g_strndup.

Release ancestry establishes the source boundary: `git describe --contains --match='5.*' 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22` returns `5.0~2624`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor` succeeds for introducer versus 5.0^{} and fails versus 4.101^{}, so the unsafe source first shipped in 5.0. This is broader than the advisory UI's explicit affected-version entry of 5.86. The fix was committed after both 5.86 and 5.87: ancestry fails for 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2 versus 5.87^{}, and `git tag --contains 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2` is empty in the validated clone, so no observed release tag contains the fix yet.

`git show --format=fuller 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2` is the direct repair: it adds `len = MIN(len, HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH);` immediately before memset/strncpy and changes no other file. Thus the advisory fix and the smallest direct fix are the same commit.

`git cat-file commit 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22` provides the BIC-only provenance check: tree 2650a41bd430d9a9acb38ece9975d5bb5630df6e, parent 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e, human author/committer Johan Hedberg, and no AI/bot marker or trailer. Any AI assistance recorded on the 2026 fix is outside the protocol's BIC-only judgment.
audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is the unbounded copy in the EIR name conversion sink, not the 2025 conversion refactor and not the 2026 fix. Line history and pickaxe agree that 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 first wrote the fixed stack array plus variable-length copy and first routed EIR names through it. Its direct parent has neither the sink nor the vulnerable route, instead rejecting invalid UTF-8 and using a bounded allocation, so parent absence is directly proven. The commit is a normal 2012 human-authored commit object with no AI disclosure or bot identity. Under the required BIC-only rule the closed verdict is therefore NOT_AI.

reasoning: The earlier ec53 refactor supplied the dangerous raw JSON header-construction primitive, but no code in afca's parent consumed X-Airbyte-Workspace-Id to choose a workspace authorization decision. afca is therefore the smallest causal BIC: in one public commit it wrote the unsafe priority rule and wired that result into workspace permission lookup, creating the authorization/resource split. The direct parent was checked and lacks both the resolver file and request-derived RBAC path. The flaw persists from the first containing release v0.50.27 through the advisory's cited v2.0.0 and in the audited release/2.1.0 and main tips; GitHub publishes no patched version, and no commit in the clone closes the raw-body workspace override, so this is genuinely unpatched and both fix fields are null. causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated member of workspace A can send a request body containing a resource identifier owned by workspace B (for example connectionId, sourceId, or destinationId) plus an otherwise undeclared workspaceId for workspace A. AuthorizationServerHandler parses the raw JSON before endpoint-schema binding and copies both values into X-Airbyte-* headers. AuthenticationHeaderResolver.resolveWorkspace gives X-Airbyte-Workspace-Id priority over all resource-derived headers, so RBAC checks the caller's permission in A while the endpoint later acts on the B resource identifier. Because no later ownership comparison binds that resource to the authorized workspace, the caller can read configuration, trigger or cancel syncs, or delete cross-workspace resources at the privilege level held in A.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The exploitable authorization mismatch first became real in afca4a0a9861af2f5f35141fad183e65f911832d. That commit added AuthenticationHeaderResolver with WORKSPACE_ID_HEADER as the first resolveWorkspace branch, ahead of connection/source/destination lookup, and changed KeycloakTokenValidator from unconditional ADMIN to request-scoped permission lookup using that resolver. It composed unsafely with the already-present raw-body-to-header extractor introduced by ec53cc9f8267b9fda31219ecc10827f6965c6f3f. The immediate parent had the extractor and workspaceId enumeration but no AuthenticationHeaderResolver and no request-header-derived workspace RBAC decision, so it lacked the specific split between authorized workspace and acted-on resource.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When the Management API is enabled with its token omitted or empty, its middleware treats every request as authenticated and its HTTP server listens on all interfaces. A remote caller can POST an arbitrary exec string to /api/v1/cron; that string is persisted as CronJob.Exec and executed by the cron scheduler through shellExecCommand with the shell command flag (-c on Unix). Scheduled execution is sufficient for RCE, and later commit c580b68716a7cdc6a0e6702e5782c17d074a7978 also added POST /api/v1/cron/{id}/exec for immediate execution. No shell metacharacter neutralization or command allowlist intervenes.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When persistent proxy memory is enabled, the proxy used the client-controlled x-headroom-user-id header verbatim as the memory partition key. That value flowed into search_memories and save/update/delete operations and into context/tool handling, without authentication or any binding between the selected partition and the caller. A client able to reach a data-plane route could therefore choose another user's identifier, retrieve that user's stored LLM memory through context/search, and write or alter memory in that partition. The flaw began on the original Anthropic memory-enabled proxy path, was later copied to OpenAI Chat Completions, Gemini, OpenAI Responses, and OpenAI websocket paths, and was practically network-reachable in the reference compose deployment because it bound the proxy to 0.0.0.0 and published port 8787 without requiring HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN. Fix 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 centralizes identity selection in resolve_memory_identity: the header is honored only for a loopback peer (or by a deployment-supplied authenticated resolver); a remote peer instead gets the configured proxy-token fingerprint or OS-user fallback. The same fix requires a proxy token in the shipped compose file.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: SPIP 4.4.20's analyse_resultat_skel() parsed each PHP block and applied an anchored header() regular expression with the PCRE m modifier. Because m makes ^ and $ match individual lines, an attacker-controlled newline followed by header("X-Spip-Filtre: intval|_request|system") inside a larger compiled PHP block was accepted as if the whole block were an intended SPIP header emission. X-Spip-Filtre was then interpreted as a pipe-delimited callable filter chain: intval produced key 0, _request read attacker-controlled POST parameter 0, and system executed that value, yielding unauthenticated remote command execution.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable product code is in upstream SPIP's spip/ecrire repository, not rapid7/metasploit-framework. On the SPIP 4.4 branch, d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d replaced the old whole-body header extractor with CollecteurPhp plus an anchored per-PHP-block /ims matcher. This was the 4.4.20 remediation for the preceding all-version RCE, but carrying m into the newly anchored matcher created the CVE-2026-77806 bypass. The Rapid7 commit referenced by the advisory, b16eca819abb8f1401f21d115e71e3dfc67b847c, only adds a Metasploit exploit module and documentation and is neither the BIC nor the fix.

X-Spip-Filtre was then interpreted as a pipe-delimited callable filter chain: intval produced key 0, _request read attacker-controlled POST parameter 0, and system executed that value, yielding unauthenticated remote command execution.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The vulnerable product code is in upstream SPIP's spip/ecrire repository, not rapid7/metasploit-framework. On the SPIP 4.4 branch, d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d replaced the old whole-body header extractor with CollecteurPhp plus an anchored per-PHP-block /ims matcher. This was the 4.4.20 remediation for the preceding all-version RCE, but carrying m into the newly anchored matcher created the CVE-2026-77806 bypass. The Rapid7 commit referenced by the advisory, b16eca819abb8f1401f21d115e71e3dfc67b847c, only adds a Metasploit exploit module and documentation and is neither the BIC nor the fix.

audit_record.reasoning: This alias points at exploit tooling, so treating b16eca819abb8f1401f21d115e71e3dfc67b847c as vulnerable code would invert causality. The smallest real BIC for the second, 4.4.20-only bypass is upstream d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d: it made the inherited m modifier security-relevant by moving matching inside each PHP block and anchoring the expression. Its immediate parent lacks that per-block multiline acceptance, even though the parent was affected by the distinct earlier RCE remediated in 4.4.20. Upstream fix 36b9847a7c14e5a069425d7d3104d22ccfecc680 removes only m, requiring the entire PHP block to be the expected header statement and closing this path in 4.4.21.
