reasoning: The vulnerable security decision first appears when PR #219 changes the session architecture from server-side cookies fixed Secure=true to client-side token-bearing cookies whose Secure flag reflects the backend request's TLS state. The public PR head decomposes the squash to one exact member with the same parent, tree, and patch, so 8bca548c78fcadc737626bea96ef1e16075792d6 is the smallest real BIC. Its immediate parent directly lacks the faulty derivation. Later repository import, refresh-token additions, reverts/reapplications, and ui-server sync commits preserve or extend the mechanism but are not origin commits. The source fix 1ed83780edfe2e395048d354976f6487b206b9db uses the browser-facing callback URL, and released sync 8876b80b63003688ab736f45ef28885695a4f6db closes the v2.53.1/v2.53.2 boundary. The BIC object has no AI marker and identifies a human author/committer, so the only evidence-permitted closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: With OAuth enabled behind a reverse proxy that terminates browser-facing HTTPS and forwards to Temporal UI Server over HTTP, authentication cookies used c.Request().TLS != nil to choose Secure. Because that request describes only the proxy-to-server hop, the server emitted the user* access/ID-token cookies and, later, refresh-token cookies without Secure even though the browser authenticated over HTTPS. Exploitation additionally requires steering the UI hostname to attacker-served HTTP, preventing HTTPS, and receiving a later same-site plaintext request while the credential is live; a malicious page alone or passive observation of the successful TLS session is insufficient.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: temporalio/ui-server PR #219 moved the OAuth user session into browser cookies. Its sole source commit 8bca548c78fcadc737626bea96ef1e16075792d6 introduced the sensitive user* cookie and set Secure from c.Request().TLS. GitHub squash commit 821cf598371353f1b579dfe1e87aeb3638b041d6 landed the identical tree and patch. The code was later imported into temporalio/ui, and the 2026 refresh-token work extended the same incorrect transport inference to a longer-lived HttpOnly refresh cookie; those moves and extensions are not the first BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When LiquidJS renders attacker-controlled template source with memoryLimit enabled, evalRangeToken meters a range as high - low + 1. A reverse range such as (100000000..1) therefore passes a large negative count to Limiter.use(); the vulnerable limiter accepts it and subtracts it from its cumulative base. Later positive allocations then satisfy base + count <= limit despite exceeding the configured budget. Repeated append operations can build a 134217728-character V8 cons-string, and replace forces flattening into a contiguous buffer, producing an uncatchable V8 fatal error and process-wide denial of service.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 2af297f81ac465feb3277ba7b92f7236409370b0 attempted to fix unmetered ranges in for tags by adding exactly ctx.memoryLimit.use(high - low + 1) to evalRangeToken, but assumed low <= high. Its direct parent already had the generic Limiter, whose signed accumulator did not reject negative counts, but did not meter ranges and therefore lacked this reverse-range counter-poisoning path. The BIC is the smallest commit in which the advisory's signed range charge and permissive limiter coexist; it is a direct one-parent change, not a move, refactor, revert, release commit, or squash aggregate.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-44645 / GHSA-8xx9-69p8-7jp3 is a CPU/event-loop denial of service in LiquidJS's renderLimit control. The for and tablerow parsers store their bodies as Template[] arrays. An empty body therefore makes each collection iteration call Render.renderTemplates([], ctx, emitter). In vulnerable releases, the only ctx.renderLimit.check(...) was inside `for (const tpl of templates)`, so an empty array executed no check while the outer for/tag or tablerow/tag loop still traversed the entire attacker-selected collection; tablerow additionally emitted table markup. A low-privileged author of an untrusted Liquid template could use an empty `{% for i in (1..N) %}{% endfor %}` or empty tablerow to consume CPU far beyond the configured time budget, bounded only by other resource controls such as memoryLimit.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 (`feat: DoS prevention, #250`). That commit introduced the renderLimit option, its Limiter state, the documented security guarantee, and the sole enforcement call in src/render/render.ts inside the per-template loop. The pre-existing Render.renderTemplates loop naturally did nothing for an empty Template[]; e443068 made that placement security-relevant by promising a per-render time limit but checking only when a body node existed. `git log e443068... -L 14,23:src/render/render.ts` attributes that exact check insertion to e443068, and `git log e443068... -S'ctx.renderLimit.check(performance.now())' -- src/render/render.ts` plus `-S'renderLimit?: number' -- src/liquid-options.ts` independently return e443068. It is a one-parent direct commit, not a move, revert, release/backport, or reconstructable squash aggregate.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: LiquidJS formed include/render/layout candidate names beneath configured root, partials, or layouts directories and then opened those names without canonicalizing them. An attacker who can place a symlink under an allowed template directory can point it at any readable file outside the directory: the lexical pathname passes the root check, Node follows the symlink during stat/read, and the external target is parsed and rendered. This affects async and sync loading and can disclose arbitrary readable content; the advisory records liquidjs <=10.25.2 as vulnerable and 10.25.3 as the first patched release.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is 8fbbec089fa4e3db4bec47462b1c08dd65c36648 (tag:include). It introduced both filesystem template loading and the include attack path: handleCache() computed path.resolve(options.root, filepath) and immediately used fs.readFileSync(filepath), while tags/include.js sent attacker-influenced include names to handleCache(). Its parent had neither renderFile/handleCache nor tags/include.js, so it could not perform this filesystem-template/symlink-following path. Later commits did not originate the flaw: b9ae479b653a34fadb98c324c4683dd1fdd31af1 split root into partials/layouts; a3455ebd0b207141c34630c0af44d917db2ca1dd added lexical startsWith containment; aebeae9e1bbb8472af7788dfd09a08cb6de58e1c merely moved that lexical check into fs.contains; and 3cd024d652dc883c46307581e979fe32302adbac extended the same non-canonical check to fallback candidates.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: LiquidJS strip_html used a regular expression that did not consume attacker-controlled HTML tags containing line terminators. For example, <img\nsrc=x\nonerror=alert(1)> survives the filter, while a browser treats the newlines as attribute whitespace and executes the event handler when the rendered result is inserted as HTML, enabling stored or reflected XSS in applications that rely on strip_html as a sanitizer.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerability began when 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2 first added strip_html using /<\/?\s*\w+\s*\/?>/g. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Preact's client renderer accepts only genuine VNodes, whose createVNode path gives them an own constructor value of exactly undefined. The regression changed the JSON-injection gate in src/diff/index.js from newVNode.constructor !== UNDEFINED to the coercive newVNode.constructor != UNDEFINED (and similarly softened related VNode checks). An attacker-controlled JSON object can therefore supply constructor:null: because null == undefined, the loose inequality is false and the gate does not reject the object. If unvalidated JSON-derived data is passed as a child/render value, an object such as {type:'span',props:{children:'Malicious'},__v:1,constructor:null} is treated as a VNode and can inject HTML, potentially script-capable markup absent CSP. The server-side preact-render-to-string path was not affected.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: A human-authored bundle-size refactor deliberately golfed strict equality checks to loose equality. The first PR member commit changed the security-sensitive constructor guard despite its adjacent 'prevent JSON-injection' comment; the second member reverted three other strict-equality changes but left this guard loose. GitHub squash-landed the two-member PR as a69aada2799626d3afbfc1eb6550611ca2444a4d.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: SRS accepts an unauthenticated RTMP publisher when vhost security is absent or disabled. A remote client on TCP/1935 can complete RTMP negotiation and a publish command without credentials; SRS returns NetStream.Publish.Start and accepts publisher traffic. Later functional media fanout permits content injection, stream-name occupation, and resource/bandwidth abuse. The referenced reporter PoC uses connect -> createStream -> publish and treats NetStream.Publish.Start as confirmation. The public report expressly says this is missing authentication/insecure default configuration, not memory corruption or code execution; therefore the NVD/GHSA arbitrary-code-execution wording is not supported by its cited technical report or by the audited source path.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated WordPress administrator with the plugin's manage_downloads capability can submit a download_path such as WP_CONTENT_DIR . '/../../etc'. Versions 1.68.11 through 1.69 compare only the uncanonicalized string prefix with WP_CONTENT_DIR, so the traversal-bearing value passes and is persisted. The Add/Edit File browser then recursively enumerates that resolved directory, an administrator can register a selected file, and the download handler concatenates the persisted base path with the selected relative name and serves it with readfile(), exposing files outside wp-content (subject to the configured per-file permission). Before 1.68.11 the setting was even less constrained and accepted arbitrary paths directly.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: a141c14127eb8d72413ac6a11dd3e7ad66aef9b1 is the smallest single-parent commit that first added the vulnerable WP_CONTENT_DIR prefix validator. Its substr($download_path, 0, strlen(WP_CONTENT_DIR)) comparison is lexical, not canonical filesystem containment, so '..' components retain the approved textual prefix while resolving outside it. The commit simultaneously identifies itself as release 1.68.11. Its immediate parent directly stores download_path and contains no prefix-validator lines; thus the specific prefix-check bypass is absent there, although the older unrestricted setting already allowed the same confidentiality impact without needing traversal.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A local attacker can create a filesystem entry whose name contains terminal control bytes such as ESC-led OSC or CSI sequences. When a victim runs the interactive TUI, marks that entry, and quits, dua-cli tears down the TUI/terminal guard and then prints each remaining marked PathBuf with println!("{}", path.display()) to stdout without encoding or filtering control characters. On an attached terminal those bytes are interpreted rather than displayed, permitting terminal-title spoofing, clipboard manipulation, and terminal-dependent integrity/confidentiality effects; ratatui's protected in-TUI rendering is bypassed because this output occurs after the TUI exits.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Feature commit 017cbd7b4c3e57e1a98fbc595159be39bc97c708 implemented issue #87's request to print marked paths on interactive exit. It simultaneously added MarkPane::into_paths(), extracted marked paths from the app, and introduced the raw post-TUI println!("{}", path.display()) sink without terminal-safe escaping. Later commits only reorganized or reformatted this already-vulnerable path.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user holding backend.manage_editor can store attacker-controlled LESS in Editor Settings -> Markup Styles (html_custom_styles). A payload such as .x { content: ~"</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>"; } makes Less_Parser preserve literal closing-style/script markup. In vulnerable releases the compiled string is emitted unescaped inside the backend-wide <style> block, so the injected script executes for later backend-page visitors. The compiled raw value is also cached, making this a stored XSS path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit c9dab67bc819b791df8432a898dd976f19388a87 reintroduced the flaw by changing modules/backend/layouts/_custom_styles.php from <?= strip_tags(EditorSetting::renderCss()) ?> to <?= EditorSetting::renderCss() ?> while ostensibly improving exception-message escaping. EditorSetting::renderCss() still returned and cached raw Less_Parser output. The immediate parent retained the output sanitizer, so this sanitizer deletion—not the 2016 feature creation, later view rename, or a release aggregate—is the smallest true BIC for the advisory's affected line.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user who can reach a list view supplied by a plugin with a Backend\Widgets\Filter numberrange scope and a conditions string can send attacker-controlled JSON numbers to onFilterUpdate(). numbersFromAjax() used /\d/ as its entire validation rule, so any string containing one digit (for example, a numeric prefix followed by SQL syntax) survived unchanged. applyScopeToQuery() then used strtr() to splice the two values into the configured conditions and passed the resulting SQL to whereRaw(), making the suffix executable SQL. The prerequisite combination is not used by built-in Winter CMS views, so a vanilla installation without such a plugin is not exploitable.

This is a direct one-parent commit, not a move, revert, backport, release commit, or squash aggregate.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A backend user granted backend.manage_branding can persist custom_css through Settings -> Customize Backend -> Styles. BrandSetting::compileCss() concatenates that value into LESS input; LESS escape syntax such as .x { content: ~"</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>"; } preserves attacker-controlled HTML delimiters in the compiled output. modules/backend/layouts/_custom_styles.php places BrandSetting::renderCss() verbatim inside a <style> element from the shared backend head/auth layouts, so the injected </style><script> sequence becomes stored script executed for later backend-page viewers. The prerequisite is trusted backend access with the specific branding permission, but the victim need only load a backend page.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 is the smallest first-writer: in modules/backend/models/BrandSettings.php it changed the LESS parse input from only the bundled custom.less file to that file concatenated with self::get('custom_css'). Its immediate parent already had the settings field, compiler, and style sink, but did not feed custom_css to the parser, so attacker-controlled markup could not reach rendered_css. The same commit also stored compiled CSS for the layout; it is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a move, revert, release carrier, or squash aggregate.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Any authenticated Winter CMS backend user could send a crafted My Account/My Settings save request for their own Backend\Models\User record and make the form behave as an administrative update form. The self-service action was deliberately exempted from backend.manage_users, while FormController treated the POST form_context value as authoritative. Selecting the update context caused normally excluded role, group, permission, and superuser fields to enter the widget save data, and the User model had no actor-aware authorization invariant before persistence. The user could therefore assign their own higher role/permissions or superuser status.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ScpClient.Download(string, DirectoryInfo) accepts C (file) and nested D (directory) record names from the remote SCP protocol stream, extracts the server-controlled filename without validation, and combines it with currentDirectoryFullName. A malicious, compromised, or MITM server can supply ../ components or an absolute/drive-qualified path so Directory.CreateDirectory or FileInfo.Open/Create operates outside the caller's destination, enabling arbitrary file creation or overwrite wherever the client process can write. Exploitation requires the victim to initiate a recursive directory download from the attacker-controlled endpoint.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the initial ScpClient feature commit: d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3 added recursive SCP download parsing and both local filesystem sinks, directly concatenating the untrusted D/C record filename below currentDirectoryFullName with no plain-name or containment check. Later commits only restyled, moved, or refactored these already-vulnerable lines.

reasoning: The vulnerability is a confused-trust execution chain: Typebot intentionally supports script blocks, but the affected embed package did not distinguish trusted author code from code arriving in an imported bot when a logged-in victim previewed it. The BIC must therefore be the first recoverable commit object that created the affected @typebot.io/js client executor, not the later async conversion, option label, path migrations, or the security patch. Mainline commit 1a3869a is a squash landing; PR #194 exposes its sole direct member 3487850b with the identical tree and parent, so decomposition is exact. The parent lacks the new package executor, satisfying direct parent absence. The advisory-linked a68f0c9 commit directly closes the preview/import trust gap, bumps 0.9.14 to 0.9.15, and is contained first by js-v0.9.15. Finally, the BIC commit object contains only a human identity and no AI marker. Under the required BIC-only rule, this is conclusively NOT_AI even though the commit is large and irrespective of any evidence outside that commit object.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An attacker-controlled imported Typebot could contain a Script block whose code was returned as a client-side action and compiled and executed by @typebot.io/js in the preview page with AsyncFunction/Function. Preview ran under the victim's authenticated app.typebot.io browser context, so the script could issue same-origin credentialed requests. It could enumerate the victim's credentials and call credentials.getCredentials to obtain decrypted OpenAI keys, Google tokens, SMTP secrets, and other stored credential data, then exfiltrate them. The user-scoped getCredentials branch did bind the record to user.id; the workspace branch checked that the victim could write the supplied workspace but fetched the credential by id without additionally binding it to that workspace. Either way, arbitrary script in the victim's session defeated the intended principal boundary. The missing control was distrust/sandboxing of imported client-executed code during privileged preview, not JavaScript syntax validation.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The affected @typebot.io/js executor lineage was created by pull-request member commit 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894. It added packages/js/src/features/blocks/logic/code/utils/executeCode.ts with Function(...args, content) and invoked it for server-supplied code actions, with no import provenance, preview trust decision, consent, or sandbox. GitHub squash commit 1a3869ae6d9fa92fc71ef9d981bfffb8e4ee4ecc has the same parent and tree, so it is only the landed aggregate object, not the smallest recoverable commit object. Later commits renamed Code to Script, added async support, moved the package/path, and exposed an Execute on client toggle defaulting true; those preserved or expanded the already-present sink rather than introducing it. A still earlier legacy bot-engine Code-step executor existed in e3e07ddd4dbae6e7b893a0d6be9f12b80d1a6c9c, but it is not the affected @typebot.io/js file/package lineage: 3487850b created the distinct V2 embed package implementation that was subsequently released as @typebot.io/js.

evidence: Advisory boundary: the assigned GHSA-4xc5-wfwc-jw47/CVE-2025-65098 record names @typebot.io/js, range `< 0.9.15`, first patched 0.9.15, the vulnerable path packages/embeds/js/src/features/blocks/logic/script/executeScript.ts, and direct commit a68f0c91790af8f52f17557f4aa202e966e7e579.

Affected sink at the fix parent: `git show a5cf298cc8043e95c6988779be8c9e0e495e0378:packages/embeds/js/src/features/blocks/logic/script/executeScript.ts` shows executeScript constructing `AsyncFunction(...args.map(id), parseContent(content))` and awaiting it in the browser, with no provenance or preview restriction. `git show a5cf298...:packages/bot-engine/src/blocks/logic/script/executeScript.ts` shows client-executed script content being emitted as `scriptToExecute` without an unsafe flag.

Credential impact at the fix parent: `git show a5cf298cc8043e95c6988779be8c9e0e495e0378:apps/builder/src/features/credentials/api/getCredentials.ts` shows authenticated plaintext decryption and return. The user branch queries `{id: input.credentialsId, userId: user.id}`. The workspace branch authorizes the supplied workspace with `isWriteWorkspaceForbidden`, but then queries credentials with `{id: input.credentialsId}` rather than `{id, workspaceId}`. Thus the advisory's broad phrase 'without ownership verification' is exact for the workspace credential lookup but not for the user branch; the malicious preview still runs as the victim and can read the victim's own secrets in both scopes.

Lineage cross-check: `git log --follow -- packages/embeds/js/src/features/blocks/logic/script/executeScript.ts` reaches landed commit 1a3869ae6d9fa92fc71ef9d981bfffb8e4ee4ecc. `git log -L 8,12:packages/embeds/js/src/features/blocks/logic/script/executeScript.ts a5cf298cc8043e95c6988779be8c9e0e495e0378` traces the client compiler/call through 96af708b, 10750f54, and 036b407a to 1a3869a. `git log -S'Function(step.options.content)()' -- packages/bot-engine/src/services/logic.ts` separately confirms the legacy e3e07ddd line and prevents confusing the old engine with this affected package lineage.

Squash decomposition: `https://api.github.com/repos/baptisteArno/typebot.io/pulls/194/commits` returns exactly one member, 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894, parent e55823e0112291a32886908fd4c63365275106e6. `git show -s --format='%H %T %P' 3487850b... 1a3869a...` yields the same tree 1c7360226886e227373c9affe2a374c1fbe7c750 and same parent for both objects. Therefore 3487850b is the recoverable direct commit and 1a3869a is the GitHub-landed squash object.

BIC change and parent absence: `git show 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894 -- packages/js/src/features/blocks/logic/code/utils/executeCode.ts packages/js/src/utils/executeLogic.ts` adds the new executor, `Function(...args.map((arg) => arg.id), content)`, and dispatches `logic.codeToExecute` to it. `git cat-file -e e55823e0112291a32886908fd4c63365275106e6:packages/js/src/features/blocks/logic/code/utils/executeCode.ts` fails because the parent has no such path; the package and affected executor are introduced by the BIC.

Why later candidates are not the BIC: 918dffb4bc7a18da41862b90288bda8fe59246ae only changed the existing runner to permit await; 42008f8c18430e6194d9552b93c8ec04ec484d6e added `isExecutedOnClient` and set its default to true while retaining the prior client path; path-changing commits such as cbc8194f19396ed8f8b3ea05d75223beeab42c3c and 10750f54d10a0d96c77371a7f244fad94471abc0 are reorganizations. The exploit does not require top-level await, so async support is not causal.

Fix behavior: `git show a68f0c91790af8f52f17557f4aa202e966e7e579` adds `enableSafetyFlags` to file import, marks imported client Script/SetVariable blocks `isUnsafe`, propagates that flag to client actions, adds `isPreview` context, and changes executeScript so preview plus unsafe code runs through runUserCodeInWorker. The added worker forces fetch credentials to `omit` and disables XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource, and nested workers. Non-imported/non-preview code retains normal execution, making this a direct trust-boundary fix rather than removal of the advertised scripting feature. The same commit bumps packages/embeds/js/package.json from 0.9.14 to 0.9.15.

Release boundary: `git rev-parse js-v0.9.14^{} js-v0.9.15^{}` resolves to c823aba3db7eb213dd762b4dc015a3a06e8b7925 and 150cbc682cc6a9dc66d19b3048318546d23086a6 respectively. a68f0c9 is not an ancestor of js-v0.9.14 but is the immediate parent of the js-v0.9.15 release commit 150cbc68. `git rev-parse js-v0.0.1^{}` resolves to ef9170dcb664705270c6859de16d92ea7c8071b7, which contains 3487850b's landed equivalent and declares @typebot.io/js version 0.0.1; therefore every released package version through 0.9.14 inherited the sink and 0.9.15 is the first fixed package release.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894` prints tree 1c736022..., parent e55823e..., human author/committer Baptiste Arnaud, and only the two-line conventional message. No AI attribution appears in the commit object. No AI evidence from the fix, PR prose, branches, or later commits was used.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: PyBlade evaluates expressions embedded in templates as Python. In the v0.1.4-alpha tag (and still in v0.1.8-alpha/v.0.1.9-alpha), PyBlade.render calls Parser.parse, whose directive handlers pass template-controlled @if/@for and other expressions to eval(..., {}, context); because the globals mapping omits __builtins__, Python inserts the normal builtins, so a template can call __import__ and execute commands. The v0.2.0-alpha rewrite keeps the vulnerability through Processor.render_variable -> ExpressionEvaluator.evaluate -> safe_eval -> eval(expression, {"__builtins__": SAFE_BUILTINS}, context); expressions containing parentheses take that direct-eval path, and Python object-model chains can recover dangerous classes/globals. The advisory's narrower claimed v0.1.8/v.0.1.9 _is_safe_ast Constant bypass is contradicted by the tagged source: for every ast.Attribute whose value is not ast.Name, including ''.__class__, the function reaches its unconditional return False, and no released engine code imports or calls sandbox.safe_eval. Thus the releases are vulnerable, but through reachable raw eval rather than the alleged AST-validation bypass, and the tracked vulnerable tag boundary is at least as early as v0.1.4-alpha.

Its direct parent b764131c740566b1f82d7c411dc13b3a804c6b8f has neither PyBladeDirectives nor an eval sink under pyblade/engine. Commit 4b193b1aa86d146eebeae442c4fd871c7a93515f subsequently wires PyBladeDirectives into PyBlade.render, so it is the activation commit, not the first writer. reasoning: CVE-2026-76844 is specifically the post-CVE-2024-29180 incomplete-fix state. The older resolver was already traversable, but e10008c is the first commit to claim containment by decoding and rejecting standalone '..' segments while retaining a character-prefix startsWith test and an offset slice. Those operations are inconsistent: '/assets../.env' has no standalone traversal segment until slicing turns the suffix into '../.env'. The immediate parent lacks that security design and belongs to the predecessor advisory; the two next-day commits are equivalent backports to other release lines, not an earlier origin. No later commit or release in the frozen clone closes the bypass. The BIC commit object is human-authored and contains no AI disclosure or AI/bot identity, so the result is NOT_AI; later fix/refactor authorship is irrelevant under the BIC-only rule.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: getFilenameFromUrl treats a textual publicPath prefix as containment. With a non-slash-terminated publicPath such as /assets, /assets../.env passes pathname.startsWith('/assets'). The 2024 UP_PATH_REGEXP guard tests path.normalize('./' + pathname), where the only '..' is embedded in the segment 'assets..' and therefore is not rejected. Slicing at publicPathPathname.length then changes the same characters into the standalone relative path '../.env'; path.join(outputPath, '../.env') escapes one directory above outputPath. The escaped file is disclosed when the selected outputFileSystem exposes physical files (not the default isolated memfs), notably writeToDisk === true or a supplied filesystem. URL parsing/normalization limits this particular bypass to one parent level; publicPath 'auto' maps to '/' and is not affected.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: This case is the incomplete fix for CVE-2024-29180, not the older unrestricted traversal itself. The original character-prefix/slice pathname construction predates 2024, but the new vulnerable security design—a decoded pathname, segment-only UP_PATH_REGEXP check, startsWith containment, and fixed-offset slice—first appears in e10008c762e4d5821ed6990348dabf0d4d93a10e on 2024-03-19. causal_chain.bug_semantics: OliveTin registered dashboard stream subscribers in a shared client collection and sent every action's execution-start, execution-finish, and output payloads to every subscriber. The subscriber's identity was retained but never checked against that action's log ACL before delivery, so a low-privilege authenticated dashboard user could receive protected action metadata, tracking IDs, usernames, live chunks, and final command output. Ordinary log APIs did enforce per-action authorization.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 first made execution output a global live broadcast: it created internal/websocket/websocket.go, registered every websocket connection in clients, and made OnExecutionFinished serialize the complete LogEntry (including Stdout and Stderr) and call broadcast, which iterated all clients without an action/user authorization decision. Its parent had action-view ACL enforcement but only a passive websocket stub and no execution-output broadcast. Commit db5de9be9793be65e2a77ab71656713f97bc779b later added the explicit Logs permission and filtered GetLogs while leaving the broadcast unfiltered; ac0f3ab6f8346157b1b2a47737ef237e0ae3af8f added globally broadcast live output chunks. The 3k API port a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 carried the existing flaw into Connect EventStream rather than originating it.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A local-auth login registers a random SID in server-side SessionStorage for about one year, and authenticated API requests accept that SID from the olivetin-sid-local cookie. Logout later expires only the browser cookie and does not delete the SID, so anyone retaining the old cookie can replay it after logout and remain authenticated until server-side expiry. The closing fix also handles OAuth2's separate registeredStates store.

audit_record.bug_semantics: A local-auth login registers a random SID in server-side SessionStorage for about one year, and authenticated API requests accept that SID from the olivetin-sid-local cookie. The closing fix also handles OAuth2's separate registeredStates store.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: With SaveLogs configured, an authenticated caller able to invoke StartAction can supply UniqueTrackingId containing slash and .. segments. The API copies that value into ExecutionRequest.TrackingID; the executor accepts any nonempty, nonduplicate string, copies it into InternalLogEntry.ExecutionTrackingID, interpolates it into the persisted log filename, and path.Join cleans the traversal before ioutil.WriteFile/os.WriteFile creates the .yaml results and .log output files outside the configured log directory. Thus the caller can select traversal-resolved destinations (subject to the fixed suffixes, generated metadata/output contents, and OliveTin process permissions).

GitHub put the identical change on the mainline as squash commit 8fd98874e2b62c693cf2ab086f6c006020507760; both objects have parent dc6f6c2896f953d2f55421df80da09bdd1926ec4 and tree abda7c392f104f1679db3dbc76bd54cea64909a5, so the PR member is the smallest reconstructable BIC rather than the squash aggregate. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The public storefront GraphQL order query accepts a caller-controlled order UUID and loads the matching order without authenticating the caller or constraining the query to the current customer or guest session. A remote unauthenticated caller who obtains a valid UUID can therefore read another customer's order and nested PII-bearing fields such as customer identity, billing/shipping addresses, purchased items, totals, payment status, and shipment data.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e is the smallest true first-writer of the authorization flaw. In packages/core/src/modules/checkout/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js it removed tokenPayload-derived customerId/sid ownership predicates from Query.order and replaced the protected order_id lookup with only query.where('uuid', '=', id). The original resolver commit 44a884b59e51d29f5022aa5b482b6c12e56ebfaa was protected, and immediate parent b398f43d4d2eedf39abf9e3658820941cbd4babd still contains that protection. Later commit 52db55816458c657a7ed49dfb27daf9f280e2169 merely removed the now-unused tokenPayload parameter, and 72d478a748e7994b46f7aecee9a849a9ef15db43 renamed the public schema argument from id to uuid; neither is the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: nltk.data.find() normalized and checked the still-encoded resource name, then passed it to urllib.request.url2pathname() while constructing a filesystem path. url2pathname() turns percent-encoded dot and separator sequences such as %2e%2e and %2f into ../ and / after the textual safety decision. A caller controlling the resource name supplied to nltk.data.find() or nltk.data.load() could therefore make the resulting path escape nltk.data.path and read any process-readable file. The attack requires an application to pass untrusted resource names into those APIs.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 51ceb7517237d78b843a95db56629b11d41ede2b changed find() from os.path.join(path_, resource_name) to os.path.join(path_, url2pathname(resource_name)) (and made the analogous zipfile-name change) to convert resource names into Windows paths. That new late decoding step is the smallest change that made a percent-encoded traversal become a real traversal at filesystem access. Its immediate parent e8c09039f8d805437a6fea14a3bce619db452eee joins the raw resource_name and does not import url2pathname, so the same encoded payload remains a literal percent-containing filename and cannot escape by this mechanism. Later raw-form checks, first introduced in 4f9ecd27897b83926119aa43e21cac3605aacfe0, did not remove the flaw because they still ran before decoding.

Later commit 1dd0432a900d85f712b26c6be07dd5f70511d868 lowercased the term and moved SQL escaping into $escapedTerm but preserved the wildcard flaw; f9a180ba8de7ca7c6742be9b3f7a32028b7c9a6b removed email from the result but also preserved enumeration of IDs/display names. Thus a7275859a5d6bc19c20827fe1ec6f6d925ea6f27, not either later edit, is the smallest reachable-history BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the authenticated WebUI RSE-management flow. A privileged attacker can create an RSE with HTML/JavaScript in city, country_name, or ISP; add_rse.js serializes those values unchanged into POST /rses/<RSE>, and the backend persists them. Later, the /rses listing supplies the server values directly to DataTables, while /rse?rse=<RSE> builds table-row HTML by concatenating the returned values into jQuery append calls. Either sink parses the stored metadata as markup, so merely viewing the listing or detail page executes attacker JavaScript in the victim's WebUI origin. The advisory notes JavaScript-readable session/API tokens and same-origin privileged requests as impact amplifiers.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Direct, single-parent feature commit 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735 added the RSE create/list/detail WebUI in new files. It simultaneously introduced the persistence path in add_rse.js, the raw DataTables listing sink in rses.js, and the raw string-concatenation table sink in rse.js; this is original vulnerable code, not a move, refactor, revert, backport, or merge carrier.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the legacy Rucio WebUI account-identity table. A privileged attacker can use Admin > Account Management > an account > Add Account Identity (POST /proxy/accounts/<account>/identities) to persist an identity such as <script>alert(document.cookie)</script>. When a victim opens /ui/account?account=<account>, load_identities() obtains the stored identity through r.list_identities() and used to pass the returned objects directly to jQuery DataTables as `data: data`; the `identity` and `type` columns were therefore rendered as HTML rather than output-encoded text. JavaScript executes in the WebUI origin with the viewing user's authority, permitting token/cookie theft or authenticated actions. The closing change constructs a separate display object and HTML-encodes identity/type with `$('<div>').text(String(value)).html()` while retaining raw `$identity`/`$type` only for API operations.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 (`[RUCIO-2849] RucioUI account admin pages`) is the smallest public first-writer. It created lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js and the account page, adding both the identity creation flow and load_identities(), whose DataTable consumed the server-returned identity objects without encoding. It is a normal one-parent feature commit, not a move, revert, release/backport, merge wrapper, or reconstructable squash; its parent had the identity-list API client but no account page, identities table, or vulnerable display sink.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The default metadata-filter converters for Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and GemFire interpolate a Filter.Key into a Lucene/query_string expression. An embedded tab, newline, carriage return, or ideographic space (U+3000) was not backslash-escaped, so attacker-controlled key text could terminate or split the intended field token and inject Boolean/query syntax. The generated string is passed to Elasticsearch/OpenSearch queryString queries (including OpenSearch delete-by-query) or to GemFire as filterQuery, permitting execution of an arbitrary query rather than the intended metadata predicate.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The earliest affected implementation is Elasticsearch support commit 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627, which created ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter.doKey and appended the trimmed metadata-prefixed key directly to the query string without syntax escaping. OpenSearch later copied the same unsafe doKey shape in 46e47849cec4b8a6fffbd13997f3cce4f886347b, and GemFire filter support introduced it in 78c5e001d39e40f0da1f5b7b2b78a38f2047c01f. March 2026 hardening routed these keys through emitLuceneString, but that helper still escaped only ordinary ASCII space and Lucene punctuation, leaving tab, LF, CR, and U+3000 exploitable until the advisory fixes.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In releases before 1.0.4, PickleScan extracted explicit GLOBAL, INST, and STACK_GLOBAL references and checked those names against a finite unsafe-global blocklist, but it did not interpret the callable/value flow produced by REDUCE. An attacker can therefore encode pkgutil.resolve_name as the only visible global, call it with a data string such as 'os:system' in a first REDUCE to obtain a blocked callable, and invoke that returned callable in a second REDUCE. Because pkgutil.resolve_name was not in the blocklist and the eventual os.system reference never appears as a pickle global, the malicious pickle had issues_count == 0 despite executing arbitrary code when unpickled. The gadget makes every blocklisted target reachable through the same indirection.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The flaw originates in the first scanner implementation, commit c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e. That commit created src/picklescan/scanner.py with an explicit _suspicious_globals blocklist, _list_globals logic limited to GLOBAL and STACK_GLOBAL, and scan_pickle_bytes logic that increments issues_count only when the extracted module/name is present in that list. pkgutil.resolve_name was neither listed nor semantically followed through REDUCE. This is the smallest repository commit that created the vulnerable security decision; it is not a move, refactor, revert, release-only commit, or squash aggregate.

reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by the browser sink, not by the longstanding ability to store a rule comment: before the BIC, the source and persistence path existed but no approval-page JavaScript consumed comments as DataTables HTML. The BIC creates that complete unsafe renderer; -S, -L, blame, and direct-parent object checks converge on it, and later edits only preserve or modify surrounding behavior. The default-branch security commit directly encodes comments before DataTables rendering, with equivalent coordinated backports establishing every advertised patch boundary. Because the BIC is a normal 2015 human-authored Gerrit commit with no explicit AI attribution or bot identity, BIC-only attribution requires NOT_AI; AI status of the 2026 fix is irrelevant.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the Rucio WebUI rule-approval flow: an authenticated low-privilege user can submit attacker-controlled HTML/JavaScript in POST /proxy/rules/ as the rule comment. The backend persists that value in the rule's comments field and list_rules returns it. approve_rules.js copied the entire server object into a DataTables data source and declared the comments property as a display column without a text renderer or output encoding, so DataTables inserted the stored value as HTML when an administrator reviewed waiting-approval rules. Script then executes in the WebUI origin, with the victim's session/API-token authority. The advisory also identifies a rule-detail viewing trigger; the directly demonstrated root sink in history is the unescaped approval-table comments column.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 010746bc16b72313d1e779fa9a15996c44b40a9f created lib/rucio/web/ui/static/approve_rules.js and, in one atomic feature commit, introduced the vulnerable chain: list_rules server data is pushed unchanged into filtered_data, passed to DataTable, and the raw {'data': 'comments'} property is displayed. The immediate parent already accepted and persisted rule comments through the REST/API/core path, but had no approve_rules.js sink, so this is the smallest first-writer rather than a later move, refactor, release commit, or squash.

reasoning: The vulnerability begins when f98f9bd89b16ab1b1b1b6366acddd1b2a4d36fe9 first adds old-format PyTorch handling and assumes the loaded magic value must appear as a literal INT/LONG opcode. The immediate parent has no such parser or scan path, and both -S and -L ancestry checks converge on this commit, so later cursor/error-handling changes are not the root introducer. Every released version from v0.0.3 through v1.0.2 carries that semantic mismatch. b9997634683a4f4bd0c7e3701e7ce7e90fe70e8c is both the direct source fix and v1.0.3 release boundary: it scans the suspicious first pickle instead of accepting a failed static extraction as a reason to stop. The introducer commit object's human identities and complete absence of AI attribution or bot markers support NOT_AI under the required BIC-only rule.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In the legacy (non-ZIP) PyTorch path, scan_pytorch validated the first pickle's magic value with get_magic_number(), which statically searched pickletools.genops() for an INT/LONG opcode. PyTorch instead unpickles that object. An attacker can make __reduce__ invoke eval to compute the correct MAGIC_NUMBER without an INT/LONG opcode, then place an RCE pickle later in the legacy stream. PyTorch accepts and executes the stream, while vulnerable scan_pytorch obtains None, raises InvalidMagicError before scanning the six-pickle stream, and reports no dangerous globals for the payload.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The original legacy-PyTorch support commit implemented semantic validation by statically extracting the first INT/LONG opcode rather than accounting for the fact that PyTorch unpickles the magic object; the same commit gated all subsequent pickle scanning on that incomplete result.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated POST to the WebUI /ui/login endpoint reaches userpass_auth(). For a nonexistent username, select_account_name() yields no ui_account and the handler immediately renders a response saying that no account is associated with that identity. For an existing username paired with a wrong password, execution instead attempts get_auth_token_user_pass() and renders a different cannot-get-auth-token response. Comparing those response bodies therefore reveals whether the supplied username exists (CWE-204); analogous distinct account/token failure responses were also present in the SAML paths.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest source commit is PR #4082 member 0f88777af4716552155edfd99731eff2571d4f7b, which created the Flask WebUI implementation, including main.py's POST /login dispatch to userpass_auth() and common/utils.py's distinct no-account and bad-token responses. GitHub later squash-landed the eight-member PR as d8f7c9e943500f0ef0fc705a200d50f436d22605 on the main lineage and e0dd5a9b9393c74fc7395d4e4970f2c31ee08ad4 on the 1.23 maintenance lineage; those squash commits are landing artifacts, not the true BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated or otherwise protocol-reachable Kyuubi client can supply a local-file URI in Spark path-bearing session/batch configuration. When kyuubi.session.local.dir.allow.list is nonempty, the server accepted the URI whenever the unnormalized uri.getPath string began with an allowed directory. An absolute path such as /allowed/../outside/secret therefore passes the textual startsWith check, but the downstream filesystem/Spark consumer resolves .. and uses a local file outside the allow list. This bypass exposes server-local files to frontend clients.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A script-controlled integer right operand reaches Boxed_Number::go for assign_remainder. In the vulnerable implementation, the assign_remainder arm executes *t_lhs %= c_rhs without first calling check_divide_by_zero(c_rhs); a zero operand therefore invokes integer remainder by zero and terminates the process with SIGFPE. The public PoC reaches this path with ret %= i when i is initially zero, including from an async script task, making this an availability flaw.

Commit 9bbe7238278f96141b51ab4c6e5313ffc2879bea shortly afterward restored guards for ordinary remainder and quotient assignment but accidentally put the intended assign-remainder guard in the assign_bitwise_and arm, so this specific regression persisted through 4804fb6e036dc325f56eecde8e875717a357e187.

Commit 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140 is the smallest first-writer because it activates user-defined function callbacks whose bodies recursively call eval_token, and its direct parent treats Function_Def as a no-op. Git -L and -S agree, while later file moves and evaluator refactors merely carry the same behavior forward. Commit 85b8e7c0c84f53c4a2467c51d8d9a3bfd7f4f90f closes the mechanism at the shared dispatcher frame entry, before native stack exhaustion, and is itself the atomic landed fix. Although that later fix commit contains Claude Opus co-author trailers, the protocol permits AI judgment only from the BIC commit object. The 2009 BIC has a human author/committer and no AI marker, so the vulnerability is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ChaiScript accepted recursively re-entering user-defined script functions without any maximum call-depth check. An attacker needs a local path to make the host evaluate supplied ChaiScript, and the resulting impact is denial of service.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ChaiScript's script-visible async() launched a callable with std::async(std::launch::async, ...) but the ChaiScript/Dispatch_Engine did not own or join the resulting worker. reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by an HTML response generator, not by the upload form itself: storage merely supplies the tainted configuration value, while the browser-facing management provider converts that value to active markup without contextual encoding. The original 2009 REST commit already created this behavior; the 2009 form rewrite, 2011/2017 moves, 2018 repository import, and later cleanup commits only preserved or relocated it. Both -S and -L identify be6b1571814721625e5e70343a2b178076d61450, and its immediate parent lacks the provider entirely. Because the BIC commit object identifies a human author/committer and contains no AI attribution or bot marker, the BIC-only rule yields NOT_AI. The null fix fields are intentional: this is an unpatched case, corroborated by the advisory's absent patched version and persistence of the sink through 7.0.26 and current HEAD.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated Administration Console user can submit attacker-controlled text in a persistent configuration attribute, demonstrated by the Deploy Application description field at POST /common/applications/uploadFrame.jsf (form:war:psection:descriptionProp:description). A later browser request to /management/domain/applications/application/ negotiates GlassFish's text/html management representation. The HTML provider reads the stored ConfigBean attribute and concatenates it into generated markup without HTML/attribute encoding; the reported payload begins with a double quote and contains , breaking out of the generated value attribute and creating an executable element. JavaScript then runs in the Administration Console origin and can read information or issue requests with the victim administrator's session.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest source commit is legacy GlassFish Git commit be6b1571814721625e5e70343a2b178076d61450 (SVN revision 26425), which first added the REST management module and v3/admin/rest/src/main/java/org/glassfish/admin/rest/provider/SingletonDomHtmlProvider.java. Its getAttributes(Dom) directly appended proxy.attribute(attribute) between HTML tags with no output encoding. Commit 881906985072f3326ed2a53d3aa2f07a2c0973f8 later moved the same unsafe value into an input value attribute, and subsequent module moves, renames, formatting, and Eclipse's 2018 Initial Contribution preserved the flaw; those are not BICs. The current descendant is nucleus/admin/rest/rest-service/src/main/java/org/glassfish/admin/rest/provider/ProviderUtil.java, where getHtmlRepresentationForAttributes passes proxy.attribute(xmlAttributeName) to getHtmlRespresentationForParameter and that method still appends parameterValue directly into value="...".

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Genkit's unauthenticated developer servers accepted requests on non-loopback interfaces without validating the HTTP Host header. A LAN peer, or a website using DNS rebinding, could invoke registered actions through the Tools/Dev UI runAction API with attacker-controlled input and context (including forged context.auth) and read the result; the telemetry trace SSE endpoint additionally widened CORS to '*', exposing action traces. CORS origin response headers were not an authorization gate.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The earliest public carrier is GitHub squash aggregate 91ed3de52e7db92943886526395ad8eac6faa77f ('Added runner, action reflection, and typed registry. (#3)'). Its message enumerates many squashed member changes, including 'Added basic Reflection API', 'Added starting of app code when starting Runner API', and 'Implemented passthrough endpoints in Runner API'. The member commit objects/parents needed to distinguish which smallest member first completed the vulnerable path are not in the public repository, so the aggregate is not recorded as the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Command_OPEN_POWERSHELL built a PowerShell -Command program by interpolating the directory of the edited file directly into a single-quoted Set-Location argument. Because an apostrophe in a Windows directory name was not escaped, a crafted path such as C:\safe'; Start-Process calc; #' terminates the string and appends attacker-chosen PowerShell. A victim need only open a file from that directory and invoke Open PowerShell or Open PowerShell as Administrator; the latter can execute after the UAC flow with elevated rights.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Atomic commit 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7 changed the pre-existing PowerShell-command skeleton from a cmd.exe /k cd invocation to powershell.exe with `-NoExit -Command "Set-Location -Path '%s'"`, passing strFolder.c_str() without PowerShell single-quote escaping. That exact semantic conversion first created the injection; the immediately preceding skeleton commit still invoked cmd.exe and therefore did not contain this PowerShell parsing flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A remote peer could open a Core-protocol connection and send FEDERATION_DOWNSTREAM_CONNECT on the dedicated federation channel before creating an authenticated session. The server trusted the packet's attacker-controlled downstream configuration, policies, credentials, and transport target, registered a connector, and deployed an outbound Core federation connection without checking the connection Subject or any federation-deployment role. A rogue broker at that outbound target could therefore inject into and/or exfiltrate from queues matched by the supplied policies. Exploitation requires untrusted inbound Core access and outbound Core reachability to an attacker-controlled target.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the original downstream-federation feature commit fb54707e2db9a6308e53a6be7f45b66129eb225f (ARTEMIS-2549): it simultaneously introduced the federation channel/message and the server-side FEDERATION_DOWNSTREAM_CONNECT handler, and the new handler deployed the requested upstream federation without authentication or authorization. This is the feature's original implementation, not a move, refactor, revert, release commit, or later regression.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When STOMP auto-create is enabled, an authenticated principal holding only SEND or CONSUME permission can request an unsupported routing type in a SEND destination-type or SUBSCRIBE subscription-type header. The vulnerable STOMP path sees the existing address, copies its routing-type set, adds the requested type, and calls ActiveMQServer.updateAddressInfo directly, bypassing the ServerSession CREATE_ADDRESS security check. Because checkRoutingSemantics runs only after this mutation, it sees the newly added type and accepts the operation. The result is an unauthorized persistent augmentation of the address routing semantics.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 intentionally added support for STOMP clients to use the same address with different routing types. Its new existing-address branch performed the update through manager.getServer().updateAddressInfo rather than the authorization-enforcing ServerSession API, creating the root authorization bypass.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: With address auto-creation disabled, an authenticated OpenWire client can request a non-durable JMS topic subscription for a nonexistent address. AMQConsumer creates a random, non-durable temporary queue on that address; the broker implicitly creates the temporary address after checking only queue-creation permission, not CREATE_ADDRESS. The unauthorized address persists until the OpenWire connection closes, when temporary resources are removed.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3 introduced Artemis's independent CREATE_ADDRESS permission and explicit address model while retaining the OpenWire non-durable-topic path that creates a temporary queue and the server queue-creation path that implicitly materializes its missing address without a CREATE_ADDRESS check. Before this commit there was no independent CREATE_ADDRESS authorization boundary to bypass.

At BIC 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3, `git show -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/security/CheckType.java` adds CREATE_ADDRESS and `git show -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/server/impl/ServerSessionImpl.java` adds the separately authorized createAddress method while createQueue still checks only CREATE_DURABLE_QUEUE/CREATE_NON_DURABLE_QUEUE before calling server.createQueue. The same commit's ActiveMQServerImpl diff implicitly adds a missing AddressInfo while creating a queue. `git log --reverse -S'CREATE_ADDRESS' -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/security/CheckType.java` identifies this as the first CREATE_ADDRESS addition.

The pre-fix OpenWire path is reproducible with `git show a2bb690e468d7956a4c83f10efa65f09a6d66f45:artemis-protocols/artemis-openwire-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/openwire/amq/AMQSession.java`: createConsumer invokes checkAutoCreateQueue only inside `if (openWireDest.isQueue())`, so topics bypass it. In AMQConsumer.createTopicSubscription, the non-durable branch creates a UUID-named queue on the requested address with durable=false and temporary=true.

Direct parent verification: `git rev-parse 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3^` returns 0bcde8140fb1f0927de58fcf856f3b449a2cdf5d; `git grep -n 'CREATE_ADDRESS' 0bcde8140fb1f0927de58fcf856f3b449a2cdf5d -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/security/CheckType.java artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/server/impl/ServerSessionImpl.java` has no match. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Bastillion's AuthFilter ran only for container-matched /manage/* and /admin/* paths, while LMVC's BaseKontroller dispatched a controller whenever the raw request URI contained the annotated controller path plus .ktrl. An unauthenticated request with an arbitrary leading segment, such as /anything/manage/viewUsers.ktrl, therefore missed AuthFilter but still dispatched the privileged controller. The same path-prefix mismatch exposed reads and state-changing manager operations, including user and managed-system creation.

Bastillion commit 65475902748be6b86a95d17b8409518697fe1e77 then replaced Struts with loophole.mvc:lmvc:1.00.00 while retaining prefix-only AuthFilter mappings, making the mismatch exploitable in Bastillion. LMVC package rename bfbfd89449b2f7441466fcbe770da57fbfd930bb and Bastillion source import fbfd6639227ee8a8f858229191c1639490a2618c preserve the line and are not BICs.

That operation first appears when proxy.php is created in dcbaefb0976cf3e9d9490455bb59504d5c807847, and its immediate parent has no proxy.php at all. causal_chain.bug_semantics: When the image proxy is enabled, an authenticated forum user can embed an attacker-chosen non-HTTPS URL in an IMG BBCode tag. SMF rewrites that URL into its own proxy.php URL and computes the required HMAC/hash with the server-side image-proxy secret, so the hash check is not an authorization boundary against that user. The proxy then performs a server-side fetch. Before the fix, destination validation was absent or limited to literal IP addresses and the exact hostname localhost; a public-looking hostname that resolved to loopback, RFC1918, link-local/cloud-metadata, or another reserved address, and redirects to such an address, reached the fetchers. This permits SSRF into services visible to the SMF host.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The root flaw was introduced by the original image-proxy endpoint in dcbaefb0976cf3e9d9490455bb59504d5c807847: proxy.php accepted a signed request URL and passed it directly to curl_fetch_web_data::get_url_data without validating the resolved destination. Follow-up commits in the same feature series supplied enabled defaults (f7a3f2b5b0bcc538637fd48ff273f094bcbc85e4), automatically signed attacker-controlled BBCode image URLs (a892a53ba45330d69b8ad8b1ede82aebaa29537b), added avatar use (d12746587bbf9b4015854677ac2a2916937116e5), and exposed settings (cc52ef5f6fae05bb41a66817758971d7a2063681). Those commits completed and broadened the attack path, but dcbaefb0976cf3e9d9490455bb59504d5c807847 is the smallest commit that first wrote the unsafe server-side fetch rather than a later move or refactor.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The advisory characterizes POST /api/v1/invitation-code/redeem as missing authentication because it accepts only an invitation code and returns SDK access and refresh tokens. The first-party design makes the single-use invitation code itself a bearer credential: an authenticated developer generates a code bound server-side to a user, and the standalone mobile app redeems that secret without a second credential. The client cannot choose a user_id at redemption. The implemented code is eight characters sampled with secrets.choice from a 32-character alphabet (32^8 about 1.1 trillion possibilities), expires after seven days, is single-use, and later active codes are revoked when replaced. Redeemed access tokens carry scope sdk. Therefore obtaining and using a valid code is possession of the intended credential, not bypassing an omitted credential; first-use theft of a leaked bearer code remains an inherent bearer-secret risk, not the claimed CWE-287/CWE-306 condition.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The reported condition originates in the intentional public bearer-code onboarding feature. PR #455 was squash-merged on main as d602dc9f01963e7e7bb9533122dc63368f4d69fd, but its reconstructable first member 8d4ae726e100f72b6687f5a5678f624631c80e8a is the smallest first-writer: it created the public redeem route, valid-code lookup, and SDK access/refresh-token issuance together. Later PR members added replacement-code revocation, tests, a dedicated expiry setting, and documentation; they did not first create the alleged missing-authentication mechanism. The project and CNA subsequently classified the report as a false positive, so there is no security-fix commit.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: On a WolfStack node still using the published built-in cluster secret, an unauthenticated remote client could send that constant in X-WolfStack-Secret. The pre-25.9.2 validate_inter_node_secret() accepted it without constraining the transport peer, and require_auth() returned the privileged synthetic identity cluster-node without a session, API key, or account. A caller reaching the management port could therefore enumerate Docker/LXC containers and invoke POST /api/containers/{runtime}/{id}/exec, whose handler passed attacker-controlled command text to sh -c inside the selected container. The 25.9.2 fix routes every presentation of the built-in default through a transport-peer gate and accepts it only from an address already recorded in nodes.json; custom per-installation secrets remain valid normally.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc (v5.9.4) is the smallest true first-writer of the hard-coded credential. It deliberately replaced the parent revision's per-node /etc/wolfstack/cluster.key loading and two-UUID random generation with the source-visible CLUSTER_SECRET constant and made load_cluster_secret() return that same value on every installation. The header gate itself came from the immediately preceding v5.9.3 commit and was not vulnerable there because its expected secret was independently generated per node. The constant was temporarily removed by the 11.26.3 hardening and restored by the 11.26.4 revert, but the revert is a later carrier/reintroduction, not the first BIC; subsequent rotation/migration work retained the built-in value as an accepted fallback on unmigrated nodes until 25.9.2.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ERC7984 stores confidential total supply in an euint64. On overflow, its mint path selects a transferred amount of zero and leaves supply unchanged rather than reverting. ERC7984ERC20Wrapper's wrap path first transfers the caller's underlying ERC-20 into the wrapper, while its ERC-1363 callback runs after the underlying transfer; both paths then call _mint and ignore the returned actual amount. Once the confidential supply is full, the transaction therefore succeeds with the underlying tokens retained but zero confidential wrapped tokens minted, causing user fund loss.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The unsafe composition first appears in PR #11 member commit 58f350da0359bc8de8d6a0a97e9ea35b664b44be: it creates ConfidentialFungibleTokenERC20Wrapper and adds both the transfer-then-_mint wrap path and the onTransferReceived _mint path without consuming or checking _mint's return value. The parent already had the intentionally non-reverting encrypted overflow behavior in ConfidentialFungibleToken, but had no ERC-20 wrapper, so the loss-of-funds mechanism did not yet exist.

reasoning: The exploit requires one coherent feature-level mistake: treating an untrusted path component as safe while forwarding a privileged Cloudflare credential and response. Commit 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65 is the smallest real source commit because it first adds every element of that attack path, and its immediate parent has no artifact API route. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /api/artifacts handler reads the attacker-controlled id query parameter, interpolates it into the path of a Cloudflare API URL, and calls fetch with the deployment's Cloudflare KV Bearer token. URL normalization resolves ../ segments before the request is sent, so a traversal such as ../../../../../../../user/tokens/verify escapes /accounts/{account}/storage/kv/namespaces/{namespace}/values/ and reaches another Cloudflare API path with the victim token; the handler then proxies the Cloudflare response to the attacker.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the initial artifact-sharing feature commit 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65, which created app/api/artifact/route.ts and in the same commit added the user-controlled id, the direct URL interpolation, the privileged Authorization header, the outbound fetch, and response proxying. Later type, TTL, and artifact-to-artifacts rename commits preserved that mechanism and are not introducers.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated request to /api/<unrecognized-provider>/<path> reaches the dynamic provider route's default branch, which calls proxyHandler. proxyHandler constructs its fetch destination directly from the attacker-controlled x-base-url header plus attacker-controlled path/query data, performs the server-side fetch without an allowlist or private/loopback-address rejection, and streams the upstream response back. An attacker can therefore make the NextChat server request arbitrary external or internal resources, including loopback and cloud metadata endpoints.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650 is the atomic first writer of the vulnerable mechanism: it adds app/api/proxy.ts with fetchUrl derived from req.headers.get("x-base-url") and fetch(fetchUrl, ...), and in the same commit changes app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts so unknown providers default to that proxyHandler. The pre-existing route instead sent its default branch to the fixed OpenAI handler, and app/api/proxy.ts did not exist in the immediate parent.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: For non-export builds, NextChat's Next.js response-header rule grants Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to the API surface. The current rule also grants every method and request header, so JavaScript from an attacker-controlled origin can pass preflight, send custom headers, and read API responses. In the reported high-impact chain, the permitted x-base-url header reaches the catch-all /api/[provider]/[...path] route; an unknown provider falls through to app/api/proxy.ts, which constructs a server-side fetch URL from x-base-url and injects the configured OpenAI key when that attacker-controlled string contains api.openai.com. The wildcard origin is the underlying CWE-346/CWE-942 flaw; wildcard methods/headers and the unauthenticated proxy amplify its consequences.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a is the smallest true BIC: it first added nextConfig.headers for non-export builds, matched /:path* (therefore including API routes), and emitted Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * plus Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Its parent e6b49a60c0eba9e591546a419eed5ed389c44b43 has no nextConfig.headers callback or CORS response headers. Commit 0fb775d71a0fac5ce4aa802bc3eb0b066c12ed7b one day later narrowed the rule to /api/:path* but amplified it by changing Allow-Methods and Allow-Headers to * and adding a 24-hour max age; it did not first create the untrusted-origin policy. Commit 6f83fbd21278c90cd978108abe54291c38ec10d7 merely moved the already-vulnerable header array into CorsHeaders and is rejected as a refactor BIC.

reasoning: The advisory covers one repeated failure to encode an identifier as one URL segment. History shows the first affected implementation was not the later AI-named advanced-payment work but the payment-refund client added in 2023. Its direct parent had empty refund placeholders, while the BIC added executable credentialed requests with raw interpolations; subsequent renames and type refactors preserve those exact vulnerable lines, and later endpoint commits only broaden the attack surface. The first containing release is 2.0.0. PR #451 introduced the intended encoder in 3.2.1 but did not touch any advisory-listed family, and 3.6.0 remains vulnerable, so fix SHAs are null rather than incorrectly treating that partial hardening as closure. The BIC commit object has a human identity and no AI marker, making NOT_AI the supported BIC-only verdict even though unrelated or non-mainline later commits mention AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The affected SDK methods insert caller-influenced identifiers directly into URL path template literals while attaching the merchant's bearer token. Slash or dot-dot content can be normalized by the WHATWG URL parser into a different API path, and a question mark can become attacker-chosen query syntax, so an application that passes an untrusted identifier without its own ownership check can make credentialed requests outside the intended resource. The affected families are payment get/capture/cancel, paymentRefund create/total/list/get, advancedPayment get/capture/cancel/update/updateReleaseDate, and disbursementRefund create/createAll/listAll.

Later additions extended the same pre-existing flaw: payment capture in 6008b53014be88d6757e89ec42688ce7d8906fe0, cancel in 0fdb24947c5f0e211d49e6d169f53b461c1dc2c3, get in 203000cd6d49d416ff8a50ca4cae290da4b92b13, refund total in 3c58ca7b51d8917681b56d5ae17265d21c047d4c, and the advancedPayment/disbursementRefund clients in adcaceaa233f5c7cb67d4723d6b7ca0cfdd25e2b. Renames and later refactors were rejected as origins.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored cross-site scripting in Telegram message search results: an attacker who can post to a shared Telegram group can store markup such as as message content. The application persists that content and later passes item.content to highlightKeyword(), which returned the raw text with only matching substrings wrapped in a span; Vue's v-html then assigned that attacker-controlled string as innerHTML. Merely rendering the result in another user's browser executes the handler. The closing change HTML-escapes message text before adding the intended highlight markup and also HTML/regex-escapes the keyword.

A local attacker can replace an intermediate directory component with a symlink after find checks the entry but before chcon resolves the pathname. chcon --no-dereference avoids following a symlink only at the final component; it still follows swapped intermediate components, so the privileged invocation can apply an attacker-chosen SELinux label to an arbitrary target such as /etc/shadow, undermining MAC integrity.

The global API authorization middleware continued immediately for a public route, the endpoint-local middleware only parsed JSON, and updateCustomer trusted request.params.id as the target UUID and spread attacker-controlled request.body into the database update without checking ownership. causal_chain.bug_semantics: tcpliveplay accepts a user-supplied pcap, obtains each packet from libpcap, rewrites its headers, and recalculates checksums. fix_all_checksum_liveplay derives the TCP checksum length solely from the untrusted IPv4 total-length/header-length fields as ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) - (iphdr->ip_hl << 2), without bounding that result by the pcap record's caplen. do_checksum_liveplay passes this length to do_checksum_math_liveplay, whose 16-bit loop reads that many bytes from the TCP-header pointer. A crafted pcap can therefore make the loop read beyond libpcap's heap packet buffer, causing the reported heap-buffer-overflow and denial of service.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first tracing places both causal components in HPE's closed appliance: an endpoint explicitly marked NO_AUTH and a controller/service path that executes the request body's cmd without an authorization or command-policy barrier. The revised hotfix closes the network path by forcing the endpoint to 404, and 11.00 is the first vendor-declared fixed release. The Rapid7 repository was linked by the advisory because it supplies exploit code; its earliest relevant commit landed three days after disclosure and its direct parent lacks the module, so treating that commit as the BIC would invert cause and proof-of-concept. Because neither the source change that introduced the HPE behavior nor the source change behind the vendor fix is publicly represented by a commit object, the smallest BIC, its immediate-parent absence, fix SHA, and BIC-only AI metadata cannot be established. This is a genuine proprietary-history boundary, so BLOCKED is more accurate than EVIDENCE_GAP and no NOT_AI/AI verdict is supportable.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: HPE OneView exposes PUT /rest/id-pools/executeCommand without authentication. The request JSON is deserialized as an ExecutableCommand; PoolController.executeCommand passes its attacker-controlled cmd property to RuntimeExecutorService.execute, which invokes Java Runtime.exec. A remote unauthenticated caller can therefore execute an arbitrary command (Rapid7 demonstrated a reverse shell as the trm3 Trusted RM Container user). Endpoint availability limits practical exposure: Rapid7 found it enabled on OneView for VMs 6.x and likely all unpatched OneView for HPE Synergy versions, while some other VM editions return 404 because ID Pools is disabled. HPE's official affected-products statement nevertheless lists all HPE OneView versions through 10.20.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable implementation is proprietary HPE OneView appliance code in guidserver.jar (com.hp.ci.mgmt.guidpools.controllers.PoolController plus RuntimeExecutorService), not code in rapid7/metasploit-framework. This repository contains a post-disclosure Metasploit exploit client and documentation only. The smallest true BIC would be the HPE source-history change that first combined unauthenticated reachability with execution of the request-controlled cmd value, but HPE's source repository and commit history are not public in the assigned evidence.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated course student (role 3) can bypass navigation/button hiding by directly loading /courses/{course-id}/settings#share or /courses/{course-id}/people?add=true. The settings route renders the restricted course configuration and share link; the people page instantiates an invitation dialog whose open state is controlled only by the user-supplied add=true query. In v0.1.13 that dialog loads organization tutors (including names/emails), exposes the student invite link and QR code, and presents add-member actions. This is an object-keyed course authorization failure: membership is accepted where an admin/tutor role check is required. The advisory demonstrates unauthorized interface/data access; successful persistence of every offered mutation was not independently established and its CVSS vector records integrity impact as none.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The disclosed lifecycle has two code origins. The earliest is the public one-parent Space merge boundary 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e, which first adds src/routes/courses/[id]/settings/+page.{js,svelte}; its CourseContainer computes isStudent, Navigation hides Settings for students, but CourseContainer unconditionally renders <slot />, so a direct URL bypasses the UI-only restriction. That commit is a squash aggregate whose message enumerates multiple CLASSROOMIO-T-90 member commits; the original member objects are absent, so it cannot be accepted as the smallest true BIC. The invite-query half is independently reconstructable: member commit 9f04d4e3a7dd3335ea8fc7db10efe78eab1431a7 first adds checkQueryParamAndOpenModal() for add=true while leaving only the Add button inside RoleBasedSecurity; it was later squashed as 82eee93417616e4dce0cec9ef30a988da07231c9. Commit 80dc3923461b21699a17157bdfdb050694fca1a5 later added the exact settings#share and people?add=true card links, but is not causal because both direct-access surfaces already existed.

reasoning: The vulnerable behavior is specifically the unsuccessful spaces-only-heading match introduced when #1281 replaced (.+) with (.*\S.*). Line history, exact-string history, the parent diff, and the identical later backport patch establish 15f8c7b2 as the smallest original causal commit and directly establish parent absence. Its commit object has only human identities and no AI marker, so the causal code is NOT_AI. This attribution is closed even though remediation is not: PR #3952 supplied a plausible direct patch in a fork, but GitHub records it as closed and unmerged, while every later upstream release tag and current develop head inspected still carry the vulnerable expression.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: getRecommendTitleFromMarkdownString applies /#{1,6} {1,}(.*\S.*)(?:\n|$)/g to renderer-supplied Markdown when the Electron main process handles save and save-as. For an unmatched heading-like line such as '#' followed by a long run of spaces and then a newline, the greedy space quantifier and the two overlapping .* quantifiers around the required non-space character explore many equivalent partitions before failing. The synchronous match therefore grows approximately quadratically and blocks the Electron main process, freezing the application. In a direct Node probe, 1,000/2,000/4,000/8,000 spaces took 0.862/3.226/12.788/50.976 ms. The source-supported trigger is malicious document content followed by a save/save-as operation; the advisory's stronger remote/no-interaction characterization is not established by these call sites.

That semantic change created the ReDoS failure path. The same patch was later replayed as dee8bb6f5b8a8e19a6e117f673c93f9dcad4aae1 on the release lineage; identical stable patch-id 6089600ebbeb76913148e7050d22a2ff06307ce0 shows that dee8bb6f is a backport/cherry-pick, not the original BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The vulnerable product is the proprietary AIT CSV Import / Export WordPress plugin, not Metasploit.
